stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 1
summaryBullets: All wisdom is from the Lord, and with him it remains forever. (1:1).
The sand of the sea, the drops of rain, and the days of eternity—who can count them? (1:2).
The height of heaven, the breadth of the earth, the abyss, and wisdom —who can search them out? (1:3).
Wisdom was created before all things and prudent understanding from eternity. (1:4).
but must also as lovers of learning be able through (1:5).
The root of wisdom—to whom has it been revealed? Her subtleties—who knows them? (1:6).
So my grandfather Jesus, who had devoted himself especially (1:7).
There is but one who is wise, greatly to be feared, seated upon his throne: the Lord. (1:8).
It is he who created her; he saw her and took her measure; he poured her out upon all his works, (1:9).
upon all the living according to his gift; he lavished her upon those who love him. (1:10).
The fear of the Lord is glory and exultation and gladness and a crown of rejoicing. (1:11).
The fear of the Lord delights the heart and gives gladness and joy and long life. (1:12).
Those who fear the Lord will have a happy end; on the day of their death they will be blessed. (1:13).
To fear the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; she is created with the faithful in the womb. (1:14).
She made among humans an eternal foundation, and among their descendants she will abide faithfully. (1:15).
To fear the Lord is fullness of wisdom; she inebriates mortals with her fruits; (1:16).
she fills their whole house with desirable goods and their storehouses with her produce. (1:17).
The fear of the Lord is the crown of wisdom, making peace and perfect health to flourish. (1:18).
She rained down knowledge and discerning comprehension, and she heightened the glory of those who held her fast. (1:19).
To fear the Lord is the root of wisdom, and her branches are long life. (1:20).
Unjust anger cannot be justified, for anger tips the scale to one’s ruin. (1:22).
Those who are patient stay calm until the right moment, and then cheerfulness comes back to them. (1:23).
They hold back their words until the right moment, and then the lips of many tell of their good sense. (1:24).
In the treasuries of wisdom is insightful analogy, but godliness is an abomination to a sinner. (1:25).
If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and the Lord will lavish her upon you. (1:26).
For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and discipline; fidelity and humility are his delight. (1:27).
Do not disobey the fear of the Lord; do not approach him with a divided mind. (1:28).
Do not be a hypocrite before others, and keep watch over your lips. (1:29).

Do not exalt yourself, or you may fall and bring dishonor upon yourself. The Lord will reveal your secrets and overthrow you before the whole congregation, because you did not come in the fear of the Lord, and your heart was full of deceit. (1:30).
to complete and publish the book (1:33).
for those living abroad who wish to gain learning and are (1:34).
preparing (1:35).
to live according to the law. (1:36).
crossRefs: Proverbs 1:7 — Fear of the Lord is beginning of knowledge.
Job 28:28 — Fear of the Lord is wisdom.
Hebrews 12:6 — The Lord disciplines whom He loves.

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 2
summaryBullets: My child, when you come to serve the Lord, prepare yourself for testing. (2:1).
Set your heart right and be steadfast, and do not be impetuous in time of calamity. (2:2).
Cling to him and do not depart, so that your last days may be prosperous. (2:3).
Accept whatever befalls you, and in times of humiliation be patient. (2:4).
For gold is tested in the fire, and those found acceptable, in the furnace of humiliation. (2:5).
Trust in him, and he will help you; make your ways straight and hope in him. (2:6).
You who fear the Lord, wait for his mercy; do not stray, or else you may fall. (2:7).
You who fear the Lord, trust in him, and your reward will not be lost. (2:8).
You who fear the Lord, hope for good things, for lasting joy and mercy. (2:9).

Consider the generations of old and see: Has anyone trusted in the Lord and been disappointed? Or has anyone persevered in the fear of the Lord and been forsaken? Or has anyone called upon him and been neglected? (2:10).
For the Lord is compassionate and merciful; he forgives sins and saves in time of distress. (2:11).
Woe to timid hearts and to slack hands and to the sinner who walks a double path! (2:12).
Woe to the fainthearted who have no trust! Therefore they will have no shelter. (2:13).
Woe to you who have lost patience! What will you do when the Lord’s reckoning comes? (2:14).
Those who fear the Lord will not disobey his words, and those who love him will keep his ways. (2:15).
Those who fear the Lord will seek his favor, and those who love him will be filled with his law. (2:16).
Those who fear the Lord will prepare their hearts and will humble themselves before him. (2:17).
Let us fall into the hands of the Lord but not into the hands of mortals, for equal to his majesty is his mercy. (2:18).
crossRefs: Proverbs 1:7 — Fear of the Lord is beginning of knowledge.
Job 28:28 — Fear of the Lord is wisdom.
Hebrews 12:6 — The Lord disciplines whom He loves.

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 3
summaryBullets: Listen to me your father, O children; act accordingly, that you may be safe. (3:1).
For the Lord honors a father above his children, and he confirms a mother’s judgment over her sons. (3:2).
Those who honor their father atone for sins, (3:3).
and those who respect their mother are like those who lay up treasure. (3:4).
Those who honor their father will have joy in their children, and when they pray they will be heard. (3:5).
Those who respect their father will have long life, and those who honor their mother obey the Lord; (3:6).
they will serve their parents as their masters. (3:7).
Honor your father by word and deed, that his blessing may come upon you. (3:8).
For a father’s blessing strengthens the houses of the children, but a mother’s curse uproots their foundations. (3:9).
Do not glorify yourself by your father’s dishonor, for your father’s dishonor is no glory to you. (3:10).
The honor of one’s father is one’s own glory, and a mother dishonored is a disgrace to her children. (3:11).
My child, help your father in his old age, and do not grieve him as long as he lives; (3:12).
even if his mind fails, be patient with him; do not despise him because you have all your faculties. (3:13).
For kindness to a father will not be forgotten and will be credited to you against your sins; (3:14).
in the day of your distress it will be remembered in your favor; like frost in fair weather, your sins will melt away. (3:15).
Whoever forsakes a father is like a blasphemer, and whoever angers a mother is cursed by the Lord. (3:16).
My child, perform your tasks with humility; then you will be loved more than a giver of gifts. (3:17).
The greater you are, the more you must humble yourself; so you will find favor in the sight of the Lord. (3:18).
For great is the might of the Lord, but by the humble he is glorified. (3:20).
Neither seek what is too difficult for you nor investigate what is beyond your power. (3:21).
Reflect upon what you have been commanded, for what is hidden is not your concern. (3:22).
In matters greater than your own affairs, do not meddle, for things beyond human understanding have been shown you. (3:23).
For their conceit has led many astray, and wrong opinion has impaired their judgment. (3:24).
Without eyes there is no light; without knowledge there is no wisdom. (3:25).
A stubborn mind will fare badly at the end, and whoever loves danger will perish in it. (3:26).
A stubborn mind will be burdened by troubles, and the sinner adds sin to sins. (3:27).
When calamity befalls the proud, there is no healing, for an evil plant has taken root in him. (3:28).
The mind of the intelligent appreciates proverbs, and an attentive ear is the desire of the wise. (3:29).
As water extinguishes a blazing fire, so almsgiving atones for sin. (3:30).
Those who repay favors give thought to the future; when they fall they will find support. (3:31).
crossRefs: Exodus 20:12 — Honor father and mother.
Luke 14:11 — Whoever exalts himself will be humbled.
James 1:27 — True religion: care for orphans and widows.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: צְדָקָה (ṣĕdāqāh) — Greek: ἐλεημοσύνη (eleēmosýnē) — Aramaic: זדקתא (zdaqātā)

stories.keyTakeaway: Honor, humility, almsgiving, and wisdom are exhorted as paths of life, while arrogance and sin bring ruin.

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 4
summaryBullets: My child, do not cheat the poor of their living, and do not keep needy eyes waiting. (4:1).
Do not grieve the hungry or anger one in need. (4:2).
Do not add to the troubles of the angry or delay giving to the needy. (4:3).
Do not reject a suppliant in distress or turn your face away from the poor. (4:4).
Do not avert your eye from the needy, and give no one reason to curse you, (4:5).
for if in bitterness of soul some should curse you, their Creator will hear their prayer. (4:6).
Endear yourself to the congregation; bow your head low to the great. (4:7).
Give a hearing to the poor, and return their greeting kindly. (4:8).
Rescue the oppressed from the oppressor, and do not be hesitant in giving a verdict. (4:9).
Be a father to orphans, and be like a husband to their mother; you will then be like a son of the Most High, and he will love you more than does your mother. (4:10).
Wisdom teaches her children and takes hold of those who seek her. (4:11).
Whoever loves her loves life, and those who seek her from early morning will be filled with joy. (4:12).
Whoever holds her fast inherits glory, and the Lord blesses the place she enters. (4:13).
Those who serve her minister to the Holy One; the Lord loves those who love her. (4:14).
Whoever obeys her will judge the nations, and whoever listens to her will live securely. (4:15).
If they remain faithful, they will inherit her; their descendants will also obtain her. (4:16).

For at first she will walk with them in disguise; she will bring fear and dread upon them and will torment them by her discipline until she trusts them, and she will test them with her ordinances. (4:17).
Then she will come straight back to them again and gladden them and will reveal her secrets to them. (4:18).
If they go astray, she will forsake them and hand them over to their ruin. (4:19).
Watch for the opportune time, and beware of evil, and do not be ashamed to be yourself. (4:20).
For there is a shame that leads to sin, and there is a shame that is glory and favor. (4:21).
Do not show partiality to your own harm or deference to your downfall. (4:22).
Do not refrain from speaking at the proper moment, and do not hide your wisdom. (4:23).
For wisdom becomes known through speech and education through the words of the tongue. (4:24).
Never speak against the truth, but be ashamed of your ignorance. (4:25).
Do not be ashamed to confess your sins, and do not try to stop the current of a river. (4:26).
Do not subject yourself to a fool or show partiality to a ruler. (4:27).
Fight to the death for truth, and the Lord God will fight for you. (4:28).
Do not be reckless in your speech or sluggish and remiss in your deeds. (4:29).
Do not be like a lion in your home or suspicious of your slaves. (4:30).
Do not let your hand be stretched out to receive and closed when it is time to give back. (4:31).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 5
summaryBullets: Do not rely on your wealth or say, “I have enough.” (5:1).
Do not follow your inclination and strength in pursuing the desires of your heart. (5:2).
Do not say, “Who can have power over me?” for the Lord will surely punish you. (5:3).
Do not say, “I sinned, yet what has happened to me?” for the Lord is slow to anger. (5:4).
Do not be so confident of forgiveness that you add sin to sins. (5:5).
Do not say, “His mercy is great; he will forgive the multitude of my sins,” for both mercy and wrath are with him, and his anger will rest on sinners. (5:6).
Do not delay to turn back to the Lord, and do not postpone it from day to day, for suddenly the wrath of the Lord will come forth, and at the time of punishment you will perish. (5:7).
Do not rely on dishonest wealth, for it will not benefit you on the day of calamity. (5:8).
Do not winnow in every wind or follow every path. (5:9).
Stand firm in what you know, and let your speech be consistent. (5:10).
Be quick to hear, and utter a reply patiently. (5:11).
If you understand, answer your neighbor, but if not, put your hand over your mouth. (5:12).
Honor and dishonor come from speaking, and the tongue of mortals may be their downfall. (5:13).
Do not be called double-tongued and do not lay traps with your tongue, for shame comes to the thief and severe condemnation to the double-tongued. (5:14).
In great and small matters cause no harm, (5:15).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 6
summaryBullets: and do not become an enemy instead of a friend, for a bad name incurs shame and reproach; so it is with the double-tongued sinner. (6:1).
Do not fall into the grip of passion, or you may be torn apart as by a bull. (6:2).
Your leaves will be devoured and your fruit destroyed, and you will be left like a withered tree. (6:3).
Strong passion destroys those who have it and makes them the laughingstock of their enemies. (6:4).
Pleasant speech multiplies friends, and a gracious tongue multiplies courtesies. (6:5).
Let those who are at peace with you be many, but let your advisers be one in a thousand. (6:6).
When you gain friends, gain them through testing, and do not trust them hastily. (6:7).
For there are friends who are such when it suits them, but they will not stand by you in time of trouble. (6:8).
And there are friends who turn to enmity and tell of the quarrel to your disgrace. (6:9).
And there are friends who are companions at the table, but they will not stand by you in time of trouble. (6:10).
When you are prosperous, they become your second self and boldly command your slaves, (6:11).
but if you are brought low, they turn against you and hide themselves from you. (6:12).
Keep away from your enemies, and be on guard with your friends. (6:13).
Faithful friends are a sturdy shelter; whoever finds one has found a treasure. (6:14).
Faithful friends are beyond price; no amount can balance their worth. (6:15).
Faithful friends are life-saving medicine, and those who fear the Lord will find them. (6:16).
Those who fear the Lord direct their friendship aright, for as they are, so are their neighbors also. (6:17).
My child, from your youth choose discipline, and when you have gray hair you will find wisdom. (6:18).
Come to her like one who plows and sows, and wait for her good harvest. For when you cultivate her you will toil but little, and soon you will eat of her produce. (6:19).
She seems very harsh to the undisciplined; fools will not remain with her. (6:20).
She will be like a heavy stone to test them, and they will not delay in casting her aside. (6:21).
For wisdom is like her name; she is not readily perceived by many. (6:22).
Listen, my child, and accept my judgment; do not reject my counsel. (6:23).
Put your feet into her fetters and your neck into her collar. (6:24).
Bend your shoulder and carry her, and do not become angry with her bonds. (6:25).
Come to her with all your soul, and keep her ways with all your might. (6:26).
Search out and seek, and she will become known to you, and when you get hold of her, do not let her go. (6:27).
For at last you will find her rest, and she will be changed into joy for you. (6:28).
Then her fetters will become for you a strong defense, and her collar a glorious robe. (6:29).
Her yoke is a golden ornament and her bonds a purple cord. (6:30).
You will wear her like a glorious robe and put her on like a splendid crown. (6:31).
If you are willing, my child, you can be disciplined, and if you apply yourself you will become clever. (6:32).
If you love to listen you will accept discipline, and if you pay attention you will become wise. (6:33).
Stand in the company of the elders. Who is wise? Attach yourself to such a one. (6:34).
Be ready to listen to every godly discourse, and let no wise proverbs escape you. (6:35).
If you see an intelligent person, rise early to visit him; let your foot wear out his doorstep. (6:36).
Reflect on the statutes of the Lord, and meditate at all times on his commandments. It is he who will give insight to your mind, and your desire for wisdom will be granted. (6:37).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 7
summaryBullets: Do no evil, and evil will never overtake you. (7:1).
Stay away from wrong, and it will turn away from you. (7:2).
Do not sow in the furrows of injustice, and you will not reap a sevenfold crop. (7:3).
Do not seek from the Lord high office or the seat of honor from the king. (7:4).
Do not assert your righteousness before the Lord or display your wisdom before the king. (7:5).
Do not seek to become a judge, or you may be unable to root out injustice; perhaps you will fear the powerful and so mar your integrity. (7:6).
Commit no offense against the public, and do not disgrace yourself among the people. (7:7).
Do not commit a sin twice; even for one you will not go unpunished. (7:8).
Do not say, “He will consider the great number of my gifts, and when I make an offering to the Most High God, he will accept it.” (7:9).
Do not grow weary when you pray; do not neglect to give alms. (7:10).
Do not ridicule a person who is embittered in spirit, for there is one who humbles and exalts. (7:11).
Do not devise a lie against your brother or do the same to a friend. (7:12).
Refuse to utter any lie, for it is a habit that results in no good. (7:13).
Do not babble in the company of the elders, and do not repeat yourself when you pray. (7:14).
Do not hate hard labor or farm work, which was created by the Most High. (7:15).
Do not enroll in the ranks of sinners; remember that retribution will not delay. (7:16).
Humble yourself to the utmost, for the punishment of the ungodly is fire and worms. (7:17).
Do not exchange a friend for money or a real brother for the gold of Ophir. (7:18).
Do not dismiss a wise and good wife, for her charm is worth more than gold. (7:19).
Do not abuse slaves who work faithfully or hired laborers who give of themselves. (7:20).
Let your soul love intelligent slaves; do not withhold from them their freedom. (7:21).
Do you have cattle? Look after them; if they are profitable to you, keep them. (7:22).
Do you have children? Discipline them, and make them obedient from their youth. (7:23).
Do you have daughters? Be concerned for their chastity, and do not show yourself too indulgent with them. (7:24).
Give a daughter in marriage, and you complete a great task, but give her to a sensible man. (7:25).
Do you have a wife who pleases you? Do not divorce her, but do not trust yourself to one whom you detest. (7:26).
With all your heart honor your father, and do not forget the birth pangs of your mother. (7:27).
Remember that it was of your parents you were born; how will you repay what they have given to you? (7:28).
With all your soul fear the Lord and revere his priests. (7:29).
With all your might love your Maker, and do not neglect his ministers. (7:30).

Fear the Lord and honor the priest, and give him his portion, as you have been commanded: the first fruits, the purification offering, the gift of the shoulders, the sacrifice of sanctification, and the first fruits of the holy things. (7:31).
Stretch out your hand to the poor, so that your blessing may be complete. (7:32).
Give graciously to all the living; do not withhold kindness even from the dead. (7:33).
Do not lag behind those who weep, but mourn with those who mourn. (7:34).
Do not hesitate to visit the sick, because for such deeds you will be loved. (7:35).
In all you do, remember the end of your life, and then you will never sin. (7:36).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 8
summaryBullets: Do not contend with the powerful, or you may fall into their hands. (8:1).
Do not quarrel with the rich, in case their resources outweigh yours, for gold has ruined many and has perverted the minds of kings. (8:2).
Do not argue with the loud of mouth, and do not heap wood on their fire. (8:3).
Do not make fun of one who is uneducated, or your ancestors may be insulted. (8:4).
Do not reproach one who is turning away from sin; remember that we all deserve punishment. (8:5).
Do not disdain one who is old, for some of us are also growing old. (8:6).
Do not rejoice over anyone’s death; remember that we must all die. (8:7).
Do not slight the discourse of the sages, but turn to their maxims, because from them you will learn discipline and how to serve the great. (8:8).
Do not ignore the discourse of the aged, for they themselves learned from their parents; from them you learn how to understand and to give an answer when the need arises. (8:9).
Do not kindle the coals of sinners, or you may be burned in their flaming fire. (8:10).
Do not let the insolent bring you to your feet, or they may lie in ambush against your words. (8:11).
Do not lend to one who is stronger than you, but if you do lend anything, count it as a loss. (8:12).
Do not give surety beyond your means, but if you give surety be prepared to pay. (8:13).
Do not go to law against a judge, for the decision will favor him because of his standing. (8:14).
Do not travel on the road with the reckless, or your troubles may become burdensome, for they will act as they please, and through their folly you will perish with them. (8:15).

Do not pick a fight with the quick-tempered, and do not journey with them through a deserted region, because bloodshed means nothing to them, and where no help is at hand they will strike you down. (8:16).
Do not consult with fools, for they cannot keep a secret. (8:17).
In the presence of strangers do nothing that is to be kept secret, for you do not know what they will divulge. (8:18).
Do not reveal your thoughts to anyone, or you may drive away your happiness. (8:19).
crossRefs: Proverbs 13:20 — Companion of fools suffers harm.
Matthew 5:27–28 — Warning against lust.
James 3:5–8 — The tongue’s power.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: רֵעַ נֶאֱמָן (rēaʿ neʾĕmān) — Greek: φίλος πιστός (phílos pistós) — Aramaic: רֵעָא מְהֵימְנָא (rēʿāʾ məhēmnāʾ)
translationNotes.note: Sirach extols the rarity and value of a true friend, contrasting with false companions.

stories.keyTakeaway: Wisdom governs speech, friendships, and desires; almsgiving and humility bring life, while pride and lust bring downfall.

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 9
summaryBullets: Do not be jealous of the wife whom you embrace, or you will teach her an evil lesson to your own hurt. (9:1).
Do not give yourself to a woman and let her trample down your strength. (9:2).
Do not go near a loose woman, or you may fall into her snares. (9:3).
Do not dally with a female singer, or you may be caught in her activities. (9:4).
Do not look intently at a virgin, or you may stumble and incur penalties for her. (9:5).
Do not give yourself to prostitutes, or you may lose your inheritance. (9:6).
Do not look around in the streets of a city or wander about in its deserted sections. (9:7).
Turn away your eyes from a shapely woman, and do not gaze at beauty belonging to another; many have been seduced by a woman’s beauty, and by it passion is kindled like a fire. (9:8).
Never dine with another man’s wife or revel with her at wine, or your heart may turn aside to her, and in blood you may plunge into destruction. (9:9).
Do not abandon old friends, for new ones cannot equal them. A new friend is like new wine; when it has aged, you will drink it with pleasure. (9:10).
Do not envy the notoriety of sinners, for you do not know what their end will be like. (9:11).
Do not delight in what pleases the ungodly; remember that they will not be held guiltless until Hades. (9:12).

Keep far from those who have power to kill, and you will not be haunted by the fear of death. But if you approach them, make no misstep, or they may rob you of your life. Know that you are stepping among snares and that you are walking on the city battlements. (9:13).
As much as you can, aim to know your neighbors, and consult with the wise. (9:14).
Let your conversation be with intelligent people, and let all your discussion be about the law of the Most High. (9:15).
Let the righteous be your dinner companions, and let your boast be in the fear of the Lord. (9:16).
A work is praised for the skill of the artisan, so a people’s leader is proved wise by his words. (9:17).
The loud of mouth are feared in their city, and the one who is reckless in speech is hated. (9:18).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 10
summaryBullets: A wise magistrate educates his people, and the rule of an intelligent person is well ordered. (10:1).
As the people’s judge is, so are his officials; as the ruler of the city is, so are all its inhabitants. (10:2).
An undisciplined king ruins his people, but a city becomes fit to live in through the understanding of its rulers. (10:3).
The government of the earth is in the hand of the Lord, and over it he will raise up the right leader for the time. (10:4).
Human success is in the hand of the Lord, and it is he who confers honor upon the lawgiver. (10:5).
Do not get angry with your neighbor for every injury, and do not resort to acts of insolence. (10:6).
Arrogance is hateful to the Lord and to mortals, and injustice is outrageous to both. (10:7).
Sovereignty passes from nation to nation on account of injustice and insolence and wealth. (10:8).
How can dust and ashes be proud? Even in life the human body is infested with worms. (10:9).
A long illness mocks the physician; the king of today will die tomorrow. (10:10).
For when humans die they inherit maggots and vermin and worms. (10:11).
The beginning of human pride is to forsake the Lord; the heart has withdrawn from its Maker. (10:12).
For the beginning of pride is sin, and the one who clings to it pours out abominations. Therefore the Lord brought upon them unheard-of calamities and destroyed them completely. (10:13).
The Lord overthrew the thrones of rulers and enthroned the lowly in their place. (10:14).
The Lord plucked up the roots of the nations and planted the humble in their place. (10:15).
The Lord laid waste the lands of the nations and destroyed them to the foundations of the earth. (10:16).
He removed some of them and destroyed them and erased the memory of them from the earth. (10:17).
Pride was not created for human beings or violent anger for those born of women. (10:18).

Whose offspring are worthy of honor? Human offspring. Whose offspring are worthy of honor? Those who fear the Lord. Whose offspring are unworthy of honor? Human offspring. Whose offspring are unworthy of honor? Those who break the commandments. (10:19).
Among family members their leader is worthy of honor, but those who fear the Lord are worthy of honor in his eyes. (10:20).
The guest and the stranger and the poor— their boast is the fear of the Lord. (10:22).
It is not right to despise one who is intelligent but poor, and it is not proper to honor one who is sinful. (10:23).
The prince and the judge and the ruler are honored, but none of them is greater than the one who fears the Lord. (10:24).
Free people will serve a wise slave, and an intelligent person will not complain. (10:25).
Do not make a display of your wisdom when you do your work, and do not extol yourself when you are in difficulty. (10:26).
Better those who work and have plenty than those who boast and lack bread. (10:27).
My child, honor yourself with humility, and give yourself the esteem you deserve. (10:28).
Who will acquit those who condemn themselves, and who will honor those who dishonor themselves? (10:29).
The poor are honored for their knowledge, while the rich are honored for their wealth. (10:30).
One who is honored in poverty, how much more in wealth! And one dishonored in wealth, how much more in poverty! (10:31).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 11
summaryBullets: The wisdom of the humble lifts their heads high and seats them among the great. (11:1).
Do not praise individuals for their good looks or loathe anyone because of appearance alone. (11:2).
The bee is small among flying creatures, but what it produces is the origin of sweet things. (11:3).
Do not mock those wearing only a loincloth or make fun of those whose day is bitter, for the works of the Lord are wonderful and his works are concealed from humans. (11:4).
Many oppressed have sat upon a throne, and one whom no one expected has worn a crown. (11:5).
Many rulers have been utterly disgraced, and the honored have been handed over to others. (11:6).
Do not find fault before you investigate; examine first and then criticize. (11:7).
Do not answer before you listen, and do not interrupt when another is speaking. (11:8).
Do not argue about a matter that does not concern you, and do not sit with sinners when they judge a case. (11:9).
My child, do not busy yourself with many matters; if you multiply activities, you will not be held blameless. If you pursue, you will not overtake, and by fleeing you will not escape. (11:10).
There are those who work and struggle and hurry but are so much the more in want. (11:11).
There are others who are slow and need help, who lack strength and abound in poverty, but the eyes of the Lord look kindly upon them; he lifts them out of their lowly condition (11:12).
and raises up their heads to the amazement of the many. (11:13).
Good things and bad, life and death, poverty and wealth, come from the Lord. (11:14).
The Lord’s gift remains with the devout, and his favor brings lasting success. (11:17).
A person becomes rich through diligence and self-denial, and the reward allotted to him is this: (11:18).
when he says, “I have found rest, and now I shall feast on my goods!” he does not realize how time passes by; he will leave them to others and will die. (11:19).
Stand by your agreement and attend to it, and grow old in your work. (11:20).
Do not wonder at the works of a sinner, but trust in the Lord and keep at your job, for it is easy in the sight of the Lord to make the poor person suddenly rich, in an instant. (11:21).
The blessing of the Lord is the reward of the pious, and quickly his blessing flourishes. (11:22).
Do not say, “What do I need, and what further benefit can be mine?” (11:23).
Do not say, “I have enough, and what harm can come to me now?” (11:24).
In the day of prosperity, adversity is forgotten, and in the day of adversity, prosperity is not remembered. (11:25).
For it is easy for the Lord on the day of death to reward individuals according to their conduct. (11:26).
An hour’s misery makes one forget delights, and at the close of one’s life one’s deeds are revealed. (11:27).
Call no one happy before his death; by how he ends, a person becomes known. (11:28).
Do not invite everyone into your home, for many are the tricks of the crafty. (11:29).
Like a decoy partridge in a cage, so is the mind of the proud, and like spies they observe your weakness, (11:30).
for they lie in wait, turning good into evil, and to worthy actions they attach blame. (11:31).
From a spark many coals are kindled, and a sinner lies in wait to shed blood. (11:32).
Beware of scoundrels, for they devise evil, and they may ruin your reputation forever. (11:33).
Receive strangers into your home, and they will stir up trouble for you and will make you a stranger to your own family. (11:34).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 12
summaryBullets: If you do good, know to whom you do it, and you will be thanked for your good deeds. (12:1).
Do good to the devout, and you will be repaid— if not by them, certainly by the Most High. (12:2).
No good comes to one who persists in evil or to one who does not give alms. (12:3).
Give to the devout, but do not help the sinner. (12:4).

Do good to the humble, but do not give to the ungodly; hold back their bread, and do not give it to them, for by means of it they might subdue you; then you will receive twice as much evil for all the good you have done to them. (12:5).
For the Most High also hates sinners and will inflict punishment on the ungodly. (12:6).
Give to the one who is good, but do not help the sinner. (12:7).
A friend is not known in prosperity, nor is an enemy hidden in adversity. (12:8).
One’s enemies are friendly when one prospers, but in adversity even one’s friend disappears. (12:9).
Never trust your enemy, for like corrosion in copper, so is his wickedness. (12:10).
Even if he humbles himself and walks bowed down, take care to be on your guard against him. Be to him like one who polishes a mirror, to be sure it does not become completely tarnished. (12:11).

Do not put him next to you, or he may overthrow you and take your place. Do not let him sit at your right hand, or else he may try to take your own seat, and at last you will acknowledge my words and be stung by what I have said. (12:12).
Who pities a snake charmer when he is bitten or all those who go near wild animals? (12:13).
So no one pities people who associate with sinners and become involved in their sins. (12:14).
They stand by you for a while, but if you falter, they will not be there. (12:15).

Enemies speak sweetly with their lips, but in their hearts they plan to throw you into a pit; enemies may have tears in their eyes, but if they find an opportunity they will never have enough of your blood. (12:16).
If evil comes upon you, you will find them there ahead of you; pretending to help, they will trip you up. (12:17).
Then they will shake their heads and clap their hands and whisper much and show their true faces. (12:18).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 13
summaryBullets: Whoever touches pitch gets dirty, and whoever associates with the proud will become like them. (13:1).
Do not lift a weight too heavy for you or associate with one mightier and richer than you. How can the clay pot associate with the iron kettle? The pot will strike against it and be smashed. (13:2).
A rich person does wrong and even adds insults; a poor person suffers wrong and must add apologies. (13:3).
Rich people will exploit you if you can be of use to them, but if you are in need they will abandon you. (13:4).
If you own something, they will live with you; they will drain your resources without a qualm. (13:5).
When they need you, they will deceive you and will smile at you and encourage you; they will speak to you kindly and say, “What do you need?” (13:6).

They will embarrass you with their delicacies, until they have drained you two or three times, and finally they will laugh at you. Should they see you afterwards, they will pass you by and shake their heads at you. (13:7).
Take care not to be led astray and humiliated when you are enjoying yourself. (13:8).
When the influential invite you, be reserved, and they will invite you more insistently. (13:9).
Do not be forward, or you may be rebuffed; do not stand aloof, or you will be forgotten. (13:10).
Do not try to treat them as equals or trust their lengthy conversations, for they will test you by prolonged talk, and while they smile they will be examining you. (13:11).
Cruel are those who do not keep your secrets; they will not spare you harm or imprisonment. (13:12).
Be on your guard and very careful, for you are walking about with your own downfall. (13:13).
Every creature loves its like and every person a neighbor. (13:15).
All living beings associate with their own kind, and people stick close to those like themselves. (13:16).
What does a wolf have in common with a lamb? No more has a sinner with the devout. (13:17).
What peace is there between a hyena and a dog, and what peace between the rich and the poor? (13:18).
Wild asses in the wilderness are the prey of lions; likewise the poor are feeding grounds for the rich. (13:19).
Humility is an abomination to the proud; likewise the poor are an abomination to the rich. (13:20).
When the rich person totters, he is supported by friends, but when the humble falls, he is pushed away by friends. (13:21).

If the rich person slips, many come to the rescue; he speaks unseemly words, but they justify him. If the humble person slips, they even criticize him; he talks sense but is not given a hearing. (13:22).
The rich person speaks, and all are silent; they extol to the clouds what he says. The poor person speaks, and they say, “Who is this fellow?” And should he stumble, they push him down. (13:23).
Riches are good if they are free from sin; poverty is evil only in the opinion of the ungodly. (13:24).
The heart changes the countenance either for good or for evil. (13:25).
The sign of a happy heart is a cheerful face, but to devise proverbs requires strenuous thinking. (13:26).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 14
summaryBullets: Happy are those who do not blunder with their lips and are not stricken with grief for sin. (14:1).
Happy are those whose hearts do not condemn them and who have not given up their hope. (14:2).
Riches are inappropriate for the small-minded, and of what use is wealth to misers? (14:3).
What they deny themselves they collect for others, and others will live in luxury on their goods. (14:4).
If they are mean to themselves, to whom will they be generous? They will not enjoy their own riches. (14:5).
No one is worse than those who are grudging to themselves; this is the repayment for their meanness. (14:6).
If ever they do good, it is by mistake, and in the end they reveal their meanness. (14:7).
Misers are evil people; they turn away and disregard people. (14:8).
The eyes of the greedy are not satisfied with their share; greedy injustice withers the soul. (14:9).
Misers begrudge bread, and it is lacking at their tables. (14:10).
My child, treat yourself well, according to your means, and present worthy offerings to the Lord. (14:11).
Remember that death does not tarry, and the decree of Hades has not been shown to you. (14:12).
Do good to friends before you die, and reach out and give to them as much as you can. (14:13).
Do not deprive yourself of a day’s enjoyment; do not let your share of desired good pass by you. (14:14).
Will you not leave the fruit of your labors to another, and what you acquired by toil to be divided by lot? (14:15).
Give and take and indulge yourself, because in Hades one cannot look for luxury. (14:16).
All living beings become old like a garment, for the decree from of old is, “You must die!” (14:17).
Like abundant leaves on a spreading tree that sheds some and puts forth others, so are the generations of flesh and blood: one dies, and another is born. (14:18).
Every work decays and ceases to exist, and the one who made it will pass away with it. (14:19).
Happy are those who meditate on wisdom and who reason intelligently, (14:20).
who reflect in their hearts on her ways and ponder her secrets, (14:21).
pursuing her like a hunter and lying in wait on her paths; (14:22).
who peer through her windows and listen at her doors; (14:23).
who camp near her house and fasten their tent pegs to her walls; (14:24).
who pitch their tents near her and so occupy an excellent lodging place; (14:25).
who place their children under her shelter and lodge under her boughs; (14:26).
who are sheltered by her from the heat and dwell in the midst of her glory. (14:27).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 15
summaryBullets: Whoever fears the Lord will do this, and whoever holds to the law will obtain wisdom. (15:1).
She will come to meet him like a mother, and like a young bride she will welcome him. (15:2).
She will feed him with the bread of understanding and give him the water of wisdom to drink. (15:3).
He will lean on her and not fall, and he will rely on her and not be put to shame. (15:4).
She will exalt him above his neighbors and will open his mouth in the midst of the assembly. (15:5).
Gladness and a crown of rejoicing and an everlasting name he will inherit. (15:6).
The foolish will not obtain her, and sinners will not see her. (15:7).
She is far from arrogance, and liars will never think of her. (15:8).
Praise is unseemly on the lips of a sinner, for it has not been sent from the Lord. (15:9).
For in wisdom must praise be uttered, and the Lord will make it prosper. (15:10).
Do not say, “It was the Lord’s doing that I fell away,” for he does not do what he hates. (15:11).
Do not say, “It was he who led me astray,” for he has no need of the sinful. (15:12).
The Lord hates all abominations; such things are not loved by those who fear him. (15:13).
It was he who created humans in the beginning, and he left them in the power of their own inclinations. (15:14).
If you choose, you can keep the commandments, and to act faithfully is a matter of your choice. (15:15).
He has placed before you fire and water; stretch out your hand for whichever you choose. (15:16).
Before each person are life and death, and whichever one chooses will be given. (15:17).
For great is the wisdom of the Lord; he is mighty in power and sees everything; (15:18).
his eyes are on those who fear him, and he knows every human action. (15:19).
He has not commanded anyone to be ungodly, and he has not given anyone permission to sin. (15:20).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 16
summaryBullets: Do not desire a multitude of worthless children, and do not rejoice in ungodly offspring. (16:1).
If they multiply, do not rejoice in them, unless the fear of the Lord is in them. (16:2).
Do not trust in their survival or rely on their numbers, for one can be better than a thousand, and to die childless is better than to have ungodly children. (16:3).
For through one intelligent person a city can be filled with people, but through a clan of outlaws it becomes desolate. (16:4).
Many such things my eye has seen, and my ear has heard things more striking than these. (16:5).
In an assembly of sinners a fire is kindled, and in a disobedient nation wrath has blazed up. (16:6).
He did not forgive the ancient giants who revolted in their might. (16:7).
He did not spare the neighbors of Lot, whom he loathed on account of their arrogance. (16:8).
He showed no pity on the doomed nation, on those dispossessed because of their sins, (16:9).
or on the six hundred thousand foot soldiers who assembled in their stubbornness. (16:10).
Even if there were only one stiff-necked person, it would be a wonder if he remained unpunished. For mercy and wrath are with the Lord; he acquits and forgives, but he also pours out wrath. (16:11).
Great as is his mercy, so also is his chastisement; he judges people according to their deeds. (16:12).
The sinner will not escape with plunder, and the patience of the godly will not be frustrated. (16:13).
He makes room for every act of almsgiving; everyone receives in accordance with his or her deeds. (16:14).
Do not say, “I am hidden from the Lord, and who from on high has me in mind? Among so many people I am unknown, for what am I in a boundless creation? (16:17).
Look, heaven and the highest heaven, the abyss and the earth tremble at his visitation! (16:18).
Together the mountains and the foundations of the earth shake and tremble when he looks upon them. (16:19).
But no human mind can grasp this, and who can comprehend his ways? (16:20).
Like a tempest that no one can see, so most of his works are concealed. (16:21).
Who is to announce his acts of justice? Or who can await them? For his decree is far off.” (16:22).
Such are the thoughts of one devoid of understanding; a senseless and misguided person thinks foolishly. (16:23).
Listen to me, my child, and acquire knowledge, and pay close attention to my words. (16:24).
I will impart discipline precisely and declare knowledge accurately. (16:25).
When the Lord created his works from the beginning and, in making them, determined their boundaries, (16:26).
he arranged their works in an eternal order and their dominion for all generations. They neither hunger nor grow weary, and they do not abandon their tasks. (16:27).
They do not crowd one another, and they never disobey his word. (16:28).
Then the Lord looked upon the earth and filled it with his good things. (16:29).
With all kinds of living beings he covered its surface, and into it they must return. (16:30).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 17
summaryBullets: The Lord created humans out of earth and makes them return to it again. (17:1).
He gave them a fixed number of days but granted them authority over everything on the earth. (17:2).
He endowed them with strength like his own and made them in his own image. (17:3).
He put the fear of them in all living beings and gave them dominion over beasts and birds. (17:4).
Discretion and tongue and eyes, ears and a mind for thinking he gave them. (17:6).
He filled them with knowledge and understanding and showed them good and evil. (17:7).
He put the fear of him into their hearts to show them the majesty of his works. (17:8).
to proclaim the grandeur of his works. (17:9).
And they will praise his holy name, (17:10).
He bestowed knowledge upon them and allotted to them the law of life. (17:11).
He established with them an eternal covenant and revealed to them his decrees. (17:12).
Their eyes saw his glorious majesty, and their ears heard the glory of his voice. (17:13).
He said to them, “Beware of all iniquity.” And he gave commandment to each of them concerning the neighbor. (17:14).
Their ways are always before him; they will not be hidden from his eyes. (17:15).
He appointed a ruler for every nation, but Israel is the Lord’s own portion. (17:17).
All their works are as the sun before him, and his eyes are ever upon their ways. (17:19).
Their iniquities are not hidden from him, and all their sins are before the Lord. (17:20).
One’s almsgiving is like a signet ring with the Lord, and he will keep a person’s kindness like the apple of his eye. (17:22).
Afterward he will rise up and repay them, and he will bring their recompense on their heads. (17:23).
Yet to those who repent he grants a return, and he encourages those who are losing hope. (17:24).
Turn back to the Lord and forsake your sins; pray in his presence and lessen your offense. (17:25).
Return to the Most High and turn away from iniquity and hate intensely what is abhorrent. (17:26).
Who will sing praises to the Most High in Hades in place of the living who give thanks? (17:27).
From the dead, as from one who does not exist, thanksgiving has ceased; those who are alive and well sing the Lord’s praises. (17:28).
How great is the mercy of the Lord and his forgiveness for those who return to him! (17:29).
For not everything is within human capability, since human beings are not immortal. (17:30).
What is brighter than the sun? Yet it can be eclipsed. So flesh and blood devise evil. (17:31).
He marshals the host of the height of heaven, but all humans are dust and ashes. (17:32).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 18
summaryBullets: He who lives forever created the whole universe; (18:1).
the Lord alone will be justified. (18:2).
To none has he given power to proclaim his works, and who can search out his mighty deeds? (18:4).
Who can measure his majestic power, and who can fully recount his mercies? (18:5).
It is not possible to diminish or increase them, nor is it possible to fathom the wonders of the Lord. (18:6).
When humans have finished, they are just beginning, and when they stop, they are still perplexed. (18:7).
What are humans, and of what use are they? What is good in them, and what is evil? (18:8).
The number of days in their life is great if they reach one hundred years. (18:9).
Like a drop of water from the sea and a grain of sand, so are a few years among the days of eternity. (18:10).
That is why the Lord is patient with them and pours out his mercy upon them. (18:11).
He sees and recognizes that their end is miserable; therefore he grants his forgiveness all the more. (18:12).

The compassion of humans is for their neighbors, but the compassion of the Lord is for every living thing. He rebukes and trains and teaches them and turns them back, as a shepherd his flock. (18:13).
He has compassion on those who accept his discipline and who are eager for his decrees. (18:14).
My child, do not mix reproach with your good deeds or harsh words with any gift. (18:15).
Does not the dew give relief from the scorching heat? So a word is better than a gift. (18:16).
Indeed, does not a word surpass a good gift? Both are to be found in a gracious person. (18:17).
A fool will rebuke ungraciously, and the gift of a grudging giver makes the eyes weary. (18:18).
Before you speak, learn, and before you fall ill, take care of yourself. (18:19).
Before judgment comes, examine yourself, and at the time of scrutiny you will find forgiveness. (18:20).
Before falling ill, humble yourself, and when you have sinned, repent. (18:21).
Let nothing hinder you from paying a vow promptly, and do not wait until death to be released from it. (18:22).
Before making a vow, prepare yourself; do not be like one who puts the Lord to the test. (18:23).
Think of his wrath on the day of death and of the moment of vengeance when he turns away his face. (18:24).
In the time of plenty think of the time of hunger; in days of wealth think of poverty and need. (18:25).
From morning to evening conditions change; all things move swiftly before the Lord. (18:26).
One who is wise is cautious in everything; when sin is all around, one guards against wrongdoing. (18:27).
Every intelligent person knows wisdom and praises the one who finds her. (18:28).
Those who are skilled in words become wise themselves and pour forth apt proverbs. (18:29).
Do not follow your base desires but restrain your appetites. (18:30).
If you allow your soul to take pleasure in base desire, it will make you the laughingstock of your enemies. (18:31).
Do not revel in great luxury, or you may become impoverished by contact with it. (18:32).
Do not become a beggar by feasting with borrowed money, when you have nothing in your purse. (18:33).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 19
summaryBullets: The one who does this will not become rich; one who despises small things will fail little by little. (19:1).
Wine and women lead intelligent men astray, and the man who consorts with prostitutes is reckless. (19:2).
Decay and worms will take possession of him, and the reckless person will be snatched away. (19:3).
One who trusts quickly has a shallow mind, and one who sins does wrong to himself. (19:4).
One who rejoices in wickedness will be condemned, (19:5).
but one who hates discussion lacks understanding. (19:6).
Never repeat a conversation, and you will lose nothing at all. (19:7).
With friend or foe do not report it, and unless it would be a sin for you do not reveal it, (19:8).
for someone may have heard you and watched you and in time will hate you. (19:9).
Have you heard something? Let it die with you. Be brave; it will not make you burst! (19:10).
Having heard something, the fool suffers birth pangs like a woman in labor with a child. (19:11).
Like an arrow stuck in a person’s thigh, so is gossip in the belly of a fool. (19:12).
Question a friend; perhaps he did not do it; or if he did, so that he may not do it again. (19:13).
Question a neighbor; perhaps he did not say it; or if he said it, so that he may not repeat it. (19:14).
Question a friend, for often it is slander; so do not believe every word. (19:15).
A person may make a slip without intending it. Who has not sinned with his tongue? (19:16).

Question your neighbor before you threaten him, and make room for the law of the Most High. ’s commandments is life-giving discipline, and those who do what is pleasing to him enjoy the fruit of the tree of immortality. (19:17).
The whole of wisdom is fear of the Lord, and in all wisdom there is the fulfillment of the law. (19:20).
The knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom, nor is there prudence in the counsel of sinners. (19:22).
There is a cleverness that is detestable, and there is a fool who merely lacks wisdom. (19:23).
Better are the God-fearing who lack understanding than the highly intelligent who transgress the law. (19:24).
There is a cleverness that is exact but unjust, and there are people who abuse favors to gain a verdict. (19:25).
There are villains bowed down in mourning, but inwardly they are full of deceit. (19:26).
They hide their faces and pretend not to hear, but when no one notices, they will take advantage of you. (19:27).
Even if lack of strength keeps them from sinning, they will nevertheless do evil when they find the opportunity. (19:28).
People will be known by their appearances, and sensible people will be known when first met face to face. (19:29).
People’s attire and hearty laughter and the way they walk proclaim things about them. (19:30).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 20
summaryBullets: There is a rebuke that is untimely, and there is the person who is wise enough to keep silent. (20:1).
How much better it is to rebuke than to fume! (20:2).
And the one who admits his fault will be kept from ridicule. (20:3).
Like a eunuch lusting to violate a young woman is the person who makes decisions under compulsion. (20:4).
Some people keep silent and are found to be wise, while others are detested for being talkative. (20:5).
Some people keep silent because they have nothing to say, while others keep silent because they know when to speak. (20:6).
The wise remain silent until the right moment, but the arrogant and the fool miss the right moment. (20:7).
Whoever talks too much is detested, and whoever pretends to authority is hated. (20:8).
There may be good fortune for a person in adversity, and a windfall may result in a loss. (20:9).
There is the gift that profits you nothing and the gift to be paid back double. (20:10).
There are losses for the sake of glory, and there are some who have raised their heads from humble circumstances. (20:11).
Some buy much for little but pay for it seven times over. (20:12).
The wise make themselves beloved by only few words, but the courtesies of fools are wasted. (20:13).
A fool’s gift will profit you nothing, for he looks for recompense sevenfold. (20:14).
He gives little and insults much; he opens his mouth like a town crier. Today he lends, and tomorrow he asks it back; such a one is hateful. (20:15).
The fool says, “I have no friends, and I get no thanks for my good deeds.” Those who eat his bread are evil-tongued. (20:16).
How many will ridicule him, and how often! (20:17).
A slip on the pavement is better than a slip of the tongue; the downfall of the wicked will occur just as speedily. (20:18).
A coarse person is like an inappropriate story, continually on the lips of the ignorant. (20:19).
A proverb from a fool’s lips will be rejected, for he does not tell it at the proper time. (20:20).
One may be prevented from sinning by poverty, so when he rests he feels no remorse. (20:21).
One may lose his life through shame or lose it because of a foolish person. (20:22).
One may make promises to a friend out of shame and so make an enemy for nothing. (20:23).
A lie is an ugly blot on a person; it is continually on the lips of the ignorant. (20:24).
A thief is preferable to a habitual liar, but both will inherit ruin. (20:25).
The character of liars leads to disgrace, and their shame is ever with them. (20:26).
Wise persons advance themselves by their words, and those who are sensible please the great. (20:27).
Those who cultivate the soil heap up their harvest, and those who please the great atone for injustice. (20:28).
Favors and gifts blind the eyes of the wise; like a muzzle on the mouth they stop reproofs. (20:29).
Hidden wisdom and unseen treasure— of what value is either? (20:30).
Better are those who hide their folly than those who hide their wisdom. (20:31).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 21
summaryBullets: Have you sinned, my child? Do so no more, but ask forgiveness for your past sins. (21:1).
Flee from sin as from a snake, for if you approach sin it will bite you. Its teeth are lion’s teeth and can destroy human lives. (21:2).
All lawlessness is like a two-edged sword; there is no healing for the wound it inflicts. (21:3).
Panic and insolence will waste away riches; thus the house of the proud will be uprooted. (21:4).
The prayer of the poor goes from their lips to the ears of God, and his judgment comes speedily. (21:5).
Those who hate reproof walk in the sinner’s steps, but those who fear the Lord repent in their heart. (21:6).
The mighty in speech are widely known; when they slip, the sensible person knows it. (21:7).
Those who build their houses with other people’s money are like those who gather stones for their own burial mounds. (21:8).
An assembly of the lawless is like a bundle of tinder, and their end is a blazing fire. (21:9).
The way of sinners is paved with smooth stones, but at its end is the pit of Hades. (21:10).
Those who keep the law control their thoughts, and the fulfillment of the fear of the Lord is wisdom. (21:11).
Those who are not clever cannot be taught, but there is a cleverness that increases bitterness. (21:12).
The knowledge of the wise will increase like a flood and their counsel like a life-giving spring. (21:13).
The mind of a fool is like a broken jar; it can hold no knowledge. (21:14).
When intelligent people hear a wise saying, they praise it and add to it; when fools hear it, they laugh at it and throw it behind their backs. (21:15).
The chatter of fools is like a burden on a journey, but delight is found in the speech of the intelligent. (21:16).
The utterance of sensible people is sought in the assembly, and they ponder their words in their minds. (21:17).
Like a house in ruins is wisdom to a fool, and the knowledge of the ignorant is meaningless talk. (21:18).
To the senseless, education is fetters on their feet and like manacles on their right hands. (21:19).
Fools raise their voices when they laugh, but the wise smile quietly. (21:20).
To the sensible, education is like a golden ornament and like a bracelet on the right arm. (21:21).
The foot of a fool rushes into a house, but an experienced person waits respectfully outside. (21:22).
A boor peers into the house from the door, but a cultivated person remains outside. (21:23).
It is ill-mannered for a person to listen at a door; the discreet would be grieved by the disgrace. (21:24).
The lips of babblers speak of what is not their concern, but the words of the prudent are weighed in the balance. (21:25).
The mind of fools is in their mouth, but the mouth of the wise is in their mind. (21:26).
When ungodly people curse an adversary, they curse themselves. (21:27).
Whisperers degrade themselves and are hated in their neighborhoods. (21:28).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 22
summaryBullets: The idler is like a filthy stone, and every one hisses at his disgrace. (22:1).
The idler is like a lump of dung; anyone who picks it up will shake it off his hand. (22:2).
It is a disgrace to be the father of an undisciplined son, and the birth of a daughter is a loss. (22:3).
A sensible daughter obtains a husband of her own, but one who acts shamefully is a grief to her father. (22:4).
An impudent daughter disgraces father and husband and is despised by both. (22:5).
Like music in time of mourning is ill-timed conversation, but a thrashing and discipline are at all times wisdom. (22:6).
Whoever teaches a fool is like one who glues potsherds together or who rouses a sleeper from deep slumber. (22:9).
Whoever tells a story to a fool tells it to a drowsy man, and at the end he will say, “What is it?” (22:10).

Weep for the dead, for they have left the light behind, and weep for the fool, for they have left intelligence behind. Weep less bitterly for the dead, for they are at rest, but the life of the fool is worse than death. (22:11).
Mourning for the dead lasts seven days, but for the foolish or the ungodly it lasts all the days of their lives. (22:12).

Do not talk much with senseless people or visit unintelligent people. Stay clear of them, or you may have trouble and be spattered when they shake themselves off. Avoid them and you will find rest, and you will never be wearied by their lack of sense. (22:13).
What is heavier than lead? And what is its name except “Fool”? (22:14).
Sand, salt, and a piece of iron are easier to bear than a stupid person. (22:15).
A wooden beam firmly bonded into a building is not loosened by an earthquake; so the mind firmly resolved after due reflection will not be afraid in a crisis. (22:16).
A mind settled on an intelligent thought is like plaster decoration that makes a wall smooth. (22:17).
Fences set on a high place will not stand firm against the wind; so a timid mind with a fool’s resolve will not stand firm against any fear. (22:18).
One who pricks the eye brings tears, and one who pricks the heart makes clear its feelings. (22:19).
One who throws a stone at birds scares them away, and one who reviles a friend destroys a friendship. (22:20).
Even if you draw your sword against a friend, do not despair, for there is a way back. (22:21).

If you open your mouth against your friend, do not worry, for reconciliation is possible. But as for reviling, arrogance, disclosure of secrets, or a treacherous blow— in these cases any friend will take to flight. (22:22).
Gain the trust of your neighbor in his poverty, so that you may rejoice with him in his prosperity. Stand by him in time of distress, so that you may share with him in his inheritance. (22:23).
The vapor and smoke of the furnace precede the fire; so insults precede bloodshed. (22:24).
I am not ashamed to shelter a friend, and I will not hide from him, (22:25).
but if harm should come to me because of him, whoever hears of it will beware of him. (22:26).
Who will set a guard over my mouth and an effective seal upon my lips, so that I may not fall because of them and my tongue may not destroy me? (22:27).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 23
summaryBullets: O Lord, Father and Master of my life, do not abandon me to their designs, and do not let me fall among them! (23:1).
Who will set whips over my thoughts and the discipline of wisdom over my mind, so as not to spare me in my errors and not overlook my sins? (23:2).
Otherwise my mistakes may be multiplied, and my sins may abound, and I may fall before my adversaries, and my enemy may rejoice over me. (23:3).
O Lord, Father and God of my life, do not give me haughty eyes, (23:4).
and remove desire from me. (23:5).
Let neither gluttony nor lust overcome me, and do not give me over to shameless passion. (23:6).
Listen, my children, to instruction concerning the mouth; the one who observes it will never be caught. (23:7).
Sinners are overtaken through their lips; by them the reviler and the arrogant are tripped up. (23:8).
Do not accustom your mouth to oaths nor habitually utter the name of the Holy One, (23:9).
for as a slave who is constantly under scrutiny will not lack bruises, so also the person who always swears and utters the Name will never be cleansed from sin. (23:10).

The one who swears many oaths is full of iniquity, and the scourge will not leave his house. If he swears in error, his sin remains on him, and if he disregards it, he sins doubly; if he swears a false oath, he will not be justified, for his house will be filled with calamities. (23:11).
There is a manner of speaking comparable to death; may it never be found in the inheritance of Jacob! Such conduct will be far from the godly, and they will not wallow in sins. (23:12).
Do not accustom your mouth to lewd ignorance, for it involves sinful speech. (23:13).

Remember your father and mother when you sit among the great, or you may forget yourself in their presence, and behave like a fool through habit; then you will wish that you had never been born, and you will curse the day of your birth. (23:14).
Those who are accustomed to using abusive language will never become disciplined as long as they live. (23:15).

Two kinds of individuals multiply sins, and a third incurs wrath. Hot passion that blazes like a fire will not be quenched until it burns itself out; those who commit incest with their near of kin will never cease until the fire burns them up. (23:16).
To the sexually immoral all bread is sweet; he will never weary until he dies. (23:17).

The one who sins against his marriage bed says to himself, “Who can see me? Darkness surrounds me, the walls hide me, and no one sees me. Why should I worry? The Most High will not remember my sins.” (23:18).

His fear is confined to human eyes, and he does not realize that the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun; they look upon every aspect of human behavior and see into hidden corners. (23:19).
Before the universe was created, it was known to him, and so it is since its completion. (23:20).
This man will be punished in the streets of the city, and where he least suspects it he will be seized. (23:21).
So it is with a woman who leaves her husband and presents him with an heir by another man. (23:22).

For, first of all, she has disobeyed the law of the Most High; second, she has committed an offense against her husband; and third, through sexual immorality she has committed adultery and brought forth children by another man. (23:23).
She herself will be brought before the assembly, and her punishment will extend to her children. (23:24).
Her children will not take root, and her branches will not bear fruit. (23:25).
She will leave behind an accursed memory, and her disgrace will never be blotted out. (23:26).
Those who survive her will recognize that nothing is better than the fear of the Lord and nothing sweeter than to heed the commandments of the Lord. (23:27).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 24
summaryBullets: Wisdom praises herself and tells of her glory in the midst of her people. (24:1).
In the assembly of the Most High she opens her mouth, and in the presence of his hosts she tells of her glory: (24:2).
“I came forth from the mouth of the Most High and covered the earth like a mist. (24:3).
I encamped in the heights, and my throne was in a pillar of cloud. (24:4).
Alone I compassed the vault of heaven and traversed the depths of the abyss. (24:5).
Over waves of the sea, over all the earth, and over every people and nation I have held sway. (24:6).
Among all these I sought a resting place; in whose inheritance should I abide? (24:7).
“Then the Creator of all things gave me a command, and my Creator pitched my tent. He said, ‘Encamp in Jacob, and in Israel receive your inheritance.’ (24:8).
Before the ages, in the beginning, he created me, and for all the ages I shall not cease to be. (24:9).
In the holy tent I ministered before him, and so I was established in Zion. (24:10).
Thus in the beloved city he gave me a resting place, and in Jerusalem was my domain. (24:11).
I took root in an honored people; in the portion of the Lord is my inheritance. (24:12).
“I grew tall like a cedar in Lebanon and like a cypress on the heights of Hermon. (24:13).
I grew tall like a palm tree in En-gedi and like rosebushes in Jericho; like a fair olive tree in the field and like a plane tree beside water I grew tall. (24:14).
Like cassia and camel’s thorn I gave forth perfume, and like choice myrrh I spread my fragrance, like galbanum, onycha, and stacte, and like the odor of incense in the tent. (24:15).
Like a terebinth I spread out my branches, and my branches are glorious and graceful. (24:16).
Like the vine I bud forth delights, and my blossoms become glorious and abundant fruit. (24:17).
“Come to me, you who desire me, and eat your fill of my fruits. (24:19).
For the memory of me is sweeter than honey and the possession of me sweeter than the honeycomb. (24:20).
Those who eat of me will hunger for more, and those who drink of me will thirst for more. (24:21).
Whoever obeys me will not be put to shame, and those who work with me will not sin.” (24:22).

All this is the book of the covenant of the Most High God, the law that Moses commanded us as an inheritance for the congregations of Jacob. Almighty alone is God, and besides him there is no savior. (24:23).
It becomes full, like the Pishon, with wisdom and like the Tigris at the time of the spring harvest. (24:25).
It fills up, like the Euphrates, with understanding, and like the Jordan at harvest time. (24:26).
It pours forth instruction like the Nile, like the Gihon at the time of vintage. (24:27).
The first man did not know wisdom fully, nor will the last one fathom her. (24:28).
For her thoughts are more abundant than the sea and her counsel deeper than the great abyss. (24:29).
I came forth like a canal from a river, like a water channel into a garden. (24:30).
I said, “I will water my garden and drench my flower beds.” And look, my canal became a river and my river a sea. (24:31).
I will again make instruction shine forth like the dawn, and I will make it clear from far away. (24:32).
I will again pour out teaching like prophecy and leave it to all future generations. (24:33).
Observe that I have not labored for myself alone but for all who seek wisdom. (24:34).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 25
summaryBullets: I take pleasure in three things, and they are beautiful in the sight of God and of mortals: agreement among brothers and sisters, friendship among neighbors, and a wife and a husband who live in harmony. (25:1).
I hate three kinds of people, and I loathe their manner of life: a pauper who boasts, a rich person who lies, and an old adulterer who lacks sense. (25:2).
If you gathered nothing in your youth, how can you find anything in your old age? (25:3).
How attractive is sound judgment in gray-haired women and for aged men to possess good counsel! (25:4).
How attractive is wisdom in the aged and understanding and counsel in the venerable! (25:5).
Rich experience is the crown of the aged, and their boast is the fear of the Lord. (25:6).
I can think of nine whom I would call happy, and a tenth my tongue proclaims: a man who can rejoice in his children, who lives to see the downfall of his foes. (25:7).
Happy the man who lives with a sensible wife and who does not plow with ox and ass together, who does not slip with the tongue and who has not become enslaved to an inferior. (25:8).
Happy is the one who finds good sense and the one who speaks to attentive listeners. (25:9).
How great is the one who finds wisdom! But none is superior to the one who fears the Lord. (25:10).
Fear of the Lord surpasses everything; to whom can we compare the one who has it? (25:11).
Any wound, but not a wound of the heart! Any wickedness, but not the wickedness of a woman! (25:13).
Any suffering, but not suffering from those who hate! And any vengeance, but not the vengeance of enemies! (25:14).
There is no venom worse than a snake’s venom and no anger worse than a woman’s wrath. (25:15).
I would rather live with a lion and a dragon than live with an evil woman. (25:16).
A woman’s wickedness changes her appearance and darkens her face like that of a bear. (25:17).
Her husband sits among the neighbors, and he cannot help sighing bitterly. (25:18).
Any iniquity is small compared to a woman’s iniquity; may a sinner’s lot befall her! (25:19).
A sandy ascent for the feet of the aged— such is a garrulous wife to a quiet husband. (25:20).
Do not be ensnared by a woman’s beauty, and do not desire a woman for her possessions. (25:21).
There is wrath and impudence and great disgrace when a wife supports her husband. (25:22).
Dejected mind, gloomy face, and wounded heart come from an evil wife. Drooping hands and weak knees come from the wife who does not make her husband happy. (25:23).
From a woman sin had its beginning, and because of her we all die. (25:24).
Allow no outlet to water and no boldness of speech to an evil wife. (25:25).
If she does not go as you direct, separate her from yourself. (25:26).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 26
summaryBullets: Happy is the husband of a good wife; the number of his days will be doubled. (26:1).
A courageous wife brings joy to her husband, and he will complete his years in peace. (26:2).
A good wife is a good portion; she will be granted as a portion to the man who fears the Lord. (26:3).
Whether rich or poor, his heart is content, and at all times his face is cheerful. (26:4).
Of three things my heart is frightened, and of a fourth I am in great fear: slander in the city, the gathering of a mob, and false accusation—all these are worse than death. (26:5).
But it is heartache and sorrow when a wife has a rival, and a tongue-lashing makes it known to all. (26:6).
A bad wife is a chafing yoke; taking hold of her is like grasping a scorpion. (26:7).
A drunken wife arouses great anger; she cannot hide her shame. (26:8).
The haughty stare betrays a sexually immoral wife; her eyelids give her away. (26:9).
Keep strict watch over a headstrong daughter, or else, when she finds liberty, she will make use of it. (26:10).
Be on guard against her impudent eye, and do not be surprised if she sins against you. (26:11).
As a thirsty traveler opens his mouth and drinks from any water near him, so she will sit in front of every tent peg and open her quiver to the arrow. (26:12).
A wife’s charm delights her husband, and her skill puts flesh on his bones. (26:13).
A silent wife is a gift from the Lord, and nothing is so precious as her self-discipline. (26:14).
A modest wife adds charm to charm, and no scales can weigh the value of her self-control. (26:15).
Like the sun rising in the heights of the Lord, so is the beauty of a good wife in her well-ordered home. (26:16).
Like the shining lamp on the holy lampstand, so is a beautiful face on a stately figure. (26:17).
Like golden pillars on silver bases, so are shapely legs upon steadfast feet. ——— (26:18).
My child, keep sound the bloom of your youth, and do not give your strength to strangers. (26:19).
Seek a fertile field within the whole plain, and sow it with your own seed, trusting in your fine stock. (26:20).
So your offspring will prosper, and, having confidence in their good descent, will grow great. (26:21).
A prostitute is regarded as spittle and a married woman as a tower of death to her lovers. (26:22).
A godless wife is given as a portion to a lawless man, but a pious wife is given to the man who fears the Lord . (26:23).
A shameless woman constantly acts disgracefully, but a modest daughter will even be embarrassed before her husband. (26:24).
A headstrong wife is regarded as a dog, but one who has a sense of shame will fear the Lord . (26:25).

A wife honoring her husband will seem wise to all, but if she dishonors him in her pride she will be known to all as ungodly. Happy is the husband of a good wife, for the number of his years will be doubled. (26:26).
A loud-voiced and garrulous wife is like a trumpet sounding the charge, and every person like this lives in the anarchy of war. ——— (26:27).

At two things my heart is grieved, and because of a third anger comes over me: a warrior in want through poverty, intelligent men who are treated contemptuously, and a man who turns back from righteousness to sin— the Lord will prepare him for the sword! (26:28).
A merchant can hardly keep from wrongdoing, nor is a tradesman innocent of sin. (26:29).

summaryBullets: Many have committed sin for gain, and those who seek to get rich will avert their eyes. (27:1).
As a stake is driven firmly into a fissure between stones, so sin is wedged in between selling and buying. (27:2).
If a person is not steadfast in the fear of the Lord, his house will be quickly overthrown. (27:3).
When a sieve is shaken, the refuse appears; so does a person’s waste when he speaks. (27:4).
The kiln tests the potter’s vessels, and the test of a person is in his conversation. (27:5).
Its fruit discloses the cultivation of a tree; so does speech the thoughts of the human mind. (27:6).
Do not praise anyone before he speaks, for this is the way people are tested. (27:7).
If you pursue justice, you will attain it and wear it like a glorious robe. (27:8).
Birds roost with their own kind, so honesty comes home to those who practice it. (27:9).
A lion lies in wait for prey; so does sin for evildoers. (27:10).
The conversation of the godly is always wise, but the fool changes like the moon. (27:11).
Among stupid people limit your time, but among thoughtful people linger on. (27:12).
The talk of fools is offensive, and their laughter is wantonly sinful. (27:13).
Their cursing and swearing make one’s hair stand on end, and their quarrels make others stop their ears. (27:14).
The strife of the proud leads to bloodshed, and their abuse is grievous to hear. (27:15).
Whoever betrays secrets destroys confidence and will never find a congenial friend. (27:16).
Love your friends and keep faith with them, but if you betray their secrets, do not follow after them. (27:17).
For as a person destroys an enemy, so you have destroyed the friendship of your neighbor. (27:18).
And as you allow a bird to escape from your hand, so you have let your neighbor go and will not catch him again. (27:19).
Do not go after him, for he is too far off and has escaped like a gazelle from a snare. (27:20).
For a wound may be bandaged, and there is reconciliation after abuse, but whoever has betrayed secrets is without hope. (27:21).
Whoever winks the eye plots harm, and those who know such a one will keep their distance. (27:22).
In your presence their mouths are all sweetness, and they admire your words, but later they will twist their speech and with your own words they will cause a scandal. (27:23).
I have hated many things but them above all; even the Lord hates them. (27:24).
Those who throw a stone straight up throw it on their own heads, and a treacherous blow opens up many wounds. (27:25).
Whoever digs a pit will fall into it, and whoever sets a snare will be caught in it. (27:26).
If people do evil, it will roll back upon them, and they will not know where it came from. (27:27).
Mockery and abuse issue from the proud, but vengeance lies in wait for them like a lion. (27:28).
Those who rejoice in the fall of the godly will be caught in a snare, and pain will consume them before their death. (27:29).
Anger and wrath, these also are abominations, yet a sinner holds on to them. (27:30).
