stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 28
summaryBullets: The vengeful will face the Lord’s vengeance, for he keeps a strict account of their sins. (28:1).
Forgive your neighbor the wrong he has done, and then your sins will be pardoned when you pray. (28:2).
Does anyone harbor anger against another and expect healing from the Lord? (28:3).
If people have no mercy toward those like themselves, can they then seek pardon for their own sins? (28:4).
If mere mortals harbor wrath, who will make an atoning sacrifice for their sins? (28:5).
Remember the end of your life and set enmity aside; remember corruption and death and be true to the commandments. (28:6).
Remember the commandments and do not be angry with your neighbor; remember the covenant of the Most High and overlook faults. (28:7).
Refrain from strife, and your sins will be fewer, for the hot-tempered kindle strife (28:8).
and the sinner disrupts friendships and sows discord among those who are at peace. (28:9).

In proportion to the fuel, so will the fire burn, and in proportion to the obstinacy, so will strife increase; in proportion to people’s strength will be their anger, and in proportion to their wealth they will increase their wrath. (28:10).
A hasty quarrel kindles a fire, and a hasty dispute sheds blood. (28:11).
If you blow on a spark, it will glow; if you spit on it, it will be put out, yet both come out of your mouth. (28:12).
Curse the gossips and the double-tongued, for they destroy the peace of many. (28:13).
Slander has shaken many and scattered them from nation to nation; it has destroyed strong cities and overturned the houses of the great. (28:14).
Slander has driven courageous women from their homes and deprived them of the fruit of their toil. (28:15).
Those who pay heed to slander will not find rest, nor will they settle down in peace. (28:16).
The blow of a whip raises a welt, but a blow of the tongue crushes the bones. (28:17).
Many have fallen by the edge of the sword, but not as many as have fallen because of the tongue. (28:18).
Happy is the one who is protected from it, who has not been exposed to its anger, who has not borne its yoke, and who has not been bound with its fetters. (28:19).
For its yoke is a yoke of iron, and its fetters are fetters of bronze; (28:20).
its death is an evil death, and Hades is preferable to it. (28:21).
It has no power over the godly; they will not be burned in its flame. (28:22).
Those who forsake the Lord will fall into its power; it will burn among them and will not be put out. It will be sent out against them like a lion; like a leopard it will mangle them. (28:23).
Look! Fence in your property with thorns, Lock up your silver and gold, (28:24).
band make a door and a bolt for your mouth. and make balances and scales for your words. (28:25).
Take care not to err with your tongue and fall victim to one lying in wait. (28:26).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 29
summaryBullets: The merciful lend to their neighbors; by holding out a helping hand they keep the commandments. (29:1).
Lend to your neighbor in his time of need; repay your neighbor when a loan falls due. (29:2).
Keep your word and be honest with him, and on every occasion you will find what you need. (29:3).
Many regard a loan as a windfall and cause trouble to those who help them. (29:4).

One kisses another’s hands until he gets a loan and is deferential in speaking of his neighbor’s money, but at the time for repayment he delays and pays back with empty promises and finds fault with the time. (29:5).

If he can pay, his creditor will hardly get back half and will regard that as a windfall. If he cannot pay, the borrower has robbed the other of his money, and he has needlessly made him an enemy; he will repay him with curses and reproaches and instead of glory will repay him with dishonor. (29:6).
Many refuse to lend, not because of meanness, but from fear of being defrauded needlessly. (29:7).
Nevertheless, be patient with someone in humble circumstances, and do not keep him waiting for your alms. (29:8).
Help the poor for the commandment’s sake, and in their need do not send them away empty-handed. (29:9).
Lose your silver for the sake of a brother or a friend, and do not let it rust under a stone and be lost. (29:10).
Lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High, and it will profit you more than gold. (29:11).
Store up almsgiving in your treasury, and it will rescue you from every disaster; (29:12).
better than a stout shield and a sturdy spear, it will fight for you against the enemy. (29:13).
A good person will be surety for his neighbor, but the one who has lost all sense of shame will fail him. (29:14).
Do not forget the kindness of your guarantor, for he has given his life for you. (29:15).
A sinner wastes the property of his guarantor, (29:16).
and the ungrateful person abandons his rescuer. (29:17).
Being surety has ruined many who were prosperous and has tossed them about like waves of the sea; it has driven the influential into exile, and they have wandered among foreign nations. (29:18).
The sinner comes to grief through surety; his pursuit of gain involves him in lawsuits. (29:19).
Assist your neighbor to the best of your ability, but be careful not to fall yourself. (29:20).
The necessities of life are water, bread, and clothing, and also a house to assure privacy. (29:21).
Better is the life of the poor under their own crude roof than sumptuous food in the house of strangers. (29:22).
Be content with little or much, and you will hear no reproach for being a guest. (29:23).
It is a miserable life to go from house to house; as a guest you should not open your mouth; (29:24).
you will play the host and provide drink without being thanked, and besides this you will hear rude words like these: (29:25).
“Come here, stranger, prepare the table; let me eat what you have there.” (29:26).
“Be off, stranger, for an honored guest is here; my brother has come for a visit, and I need the house.” (29:27).
It is hard for a sensible person to bear scolding about lodging and the insults of the moneylender. (29:28).

summaryBullets: He who loves his son will whip him often, so that he may rejoice at the way he turns out. (30:1).
He who disciplines his son will profit by him and will boast of him among acquaintances. (30:2).
He who teaches his son will make his enemies envious and will glory in him among his friends. (30:3).
When the father dies, he will not seem to be dead, for he has left behind him one like himself, (30:4).
whom in his life he looked upon with joy and at death, without grief. (30:5).
He has left behind him an avenger against his enemies and one to repay the kindness of his friends. (30:6).
Whoever cherishes his son will bind up his wounds, and at every cry his heart will be troubled. (30:7).
An unbroken horse turns out stubborn, and an unchecked son turns out headstrong. (30:8).
Pamper a child, and he will terrorize you; play with him, and he will grieve you. (30:9).
Do not laugh with him, or you will have sorrow with him, and in the end you will gnash your teeth. (30:10).
Give him no freedom in his youth; (30:11).
beat his sides while he is young, or else he will become stubborn and disobey you. (30:12).
Discipline your son and make his yoke heavy, so that you may not be offended by his shamelessness. (30:13).
Better off poor, healthy, and fit than rich and afflicted in body. (30:14).
Health and fitness are better than any gold and a robust body than countless riches. (30:15).
There is no wealth better than health of body and no gladness above joy of heart. (30:16).
Death is better than a life of misery and eternal sleep than chronic sickness. (30:17).
Good things poured out upon a mouth that is closed are like offerings of food placed upon a grave. (30:18).
Of what use to an idol is a sacrifice? For it can neither eat nor smell. So is the one punished by the Lord; (30:19).
he sees with his eyes and groans as a eunuch groans when embracing a young woman. (30:20).
Do not give yourself over to sorrow, and do not distress yourself deliberately. (30:21).
A joyful heart is life itself, and rejoicing lengthens one’s life span. (30:22).
Indulge yourself and take comfort, and remove sorrow far from you, for sorrow has destroyed many, and no advantage ever comes from it. (30:23).
Jealousy and anger shorten life, and anxiety brings on premature old age. (30:24).
Those who are cheerful and merry at table will benefit from their food. (30:25).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 31
summaryBullets: Wakefulness over wealth wastes away one’s flesh, and anxiety about it drives away sleep. (31:1).
Wakeful anxiety prevents slumber, and a severe illness carries off sleep. (31:2).
Rich people toil to amass possessions, and when they rest, they fill themselves with their delicacies. (31:3).
Poor people toil to make a meager living, and if ever they rest, they become needy. (31:4).
Those who love gold will not be justified; those who pursue money will be led astray by it. (31:5).
Many have come to ruin because of gold, and their destruction has met them face to face. (31:6).
It is a stumbling block to those who are avid for it, and every fool will be taken captive by it. (31:7).
Blessed are the rich who are found blameless and who do not go after gold. (31:8).
Who are they, that we may call them happy? For they have done wonders among their people. (31:9).
Who has been tested by it and been found perfect? Let it be for them a ground for boasting. Who has had the power to transgress and did not transgress and to do evil and did not do it? (31:10).
Their prosperity will be established, and the assembly will proclaim their acts of charity. (31:11).
Are you seated at the table of the great? Do not be greedy at it, and do not say, “How much food there is here!” (31:12).
Remember that a greedy eye is a bad thing. What has been created more greedy than the eye? Therefore it covers the face with tears. (31:13).
Do not reach out your hand for everything you see, and do not crowd your neighbor at the dish. (31:14).
Judge your neighbor’s feelings by your own, and in every matter be thoughtful. (31:15).
Eat what is set before you like a well brought-up person, and do not chew greedily, or you will be despised. (31:16).
Be the first to stop, as befits good manners, and do not be insatiable, or you will give offense. (31:17).
If you are seated among many persons, do not help yourself before they do. (31:18).
How ample a little is for the well-disciplined! They do not breathe heavily when in bed. (31:19).
Healthy sleep depends on moderate eating; they rise early and feel fit. The distress of sleeplessness and of nausea and colic are with the glutton. (31:20).
If you are overstuffed with food, get up to vomit, and you will have relief. (31:21).
Listen to me, my child, and do not disregard me, and in the end you will appreciate my words. In everything you do be moderate, and no sickness will overtake you. (31:22).
People bless those who are liberal with food, and the testimony to their generosity is trustworthy. (31:23).
The city complains of those who are stingy with food, and the testimony to their stinginess is accurate. (31:24).
Do not try to prove your strength by wine-drinking, for wine has destroyed many. (31:25).
As the furnace tests the work of the smith, so wine tests hearts when the insolent quarrel. (31:26).
Wine is very life to humans if taken in moderation. What is life to one who is without wine? It has been created to make people happy. (31:27).
Wine drunk at the proper time and in moderation is rejoicing of heart and gladness of soul. (31:28).
Wine drunk to excess leads to bitterness of spirit, to quarrels and stumbling. (31:29).
Drunkenness increases the anger of fools to their own hurt, reducing their strength and adding wounds. (31:30).
Do not reprove your neighbors at a banquet of wine, and do not despise them in their merrymaking; speak no word of reproach to them, and do not distress them by making demands of them. (31:31).

summaryBullets: If they make you master of the feast, do not exalt yourself; be among them as one of their number. Take care of them first and then sit down; (32:1).
when you have fulfilled all your duties, take your place, so that you may be merry along with them and receive a wreath for your excellent leadership. (32:2).
Speak, you who are older, for it is your right, but with accurate knowledge, and do not interrupt the music. (32:3).
Where there is entertainment, do not pour out talk; do not display your cleverness at the wrong time. (32:4).
A ruby seal in a setting of gold is a concert of music at a banquet of wine. (32:5).
A seal of emerald in a rich setting of gold is the melody of music with good wine. (32:6).
Speak, you who are young, if you are obliged to, but no more than twice and only if asked. (32:7).
Be brief; say much in few words; be as one who knows and can still hold his tongue. (32:8).
Among the great do not act as their equal; and when another is speaking, do not babble. (32:9).
Lightning travels ahead of the thunder, and approval goes before one who is modest. (32:10).
Leave in good time and do not be the last; go home quickly and do not linger. (32:11).
Amuse yourself there to your heart’s content, but do not sin through proud speech. (32:12).
But above all bless your Maker, who intoxicates you with his good gifts. (32:13).
The one who seeks God will accept his discipline, and those who rise early to seek him will find favor. (32:14).
The one who seeks the law will be filled with it, but the hypocrite will stumble at it. (32:15).
Those who fear the Lord will form true judgments, and they will kindle righteous deeds like a light. (32:16).
Sinners will shun reproof and will find a decision according to their liking. (32:17).
A sensible person will not overlook a thoughtful suggestion; an insolent and proud person will not be deterred by fear. (32:18).
Do nothing without deliberation, but when you have acted do not regret it. (32:19).
Do not go on a path full of hazards, and do not stumble at an obstacle twice. (32:20).
Do not be overconfident on a smooth road, (32:21).
and give good heed to your paths. (32:22).
Guard yourself in every act, for this is the keeping of the commandments. (32:23).
The one who keeps the law preserves himself, and the one who trusts the Lord will not suffer loss. (32:24).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 33
summaryBullets: No evil will befall the one who fears the Lord, but in trials such a one will be rescued again and again. (33:1).
The wise will not hate the law, but the one who is hypocritical about it is like a boat in a storm. (33:2).
The sensible person will trust in the law, for such a one the law is as dependable as a divine oracle. (33:3).
Prepare what to say, and then you will be listened to; draw upon your training and give your answer. (33:4).
The heart of a fool is like a cart wheel and his thoughts like a turning axle. (33:5).
A mocking friend is like a stallion that neighs no matter who the rider is. (33:6).
Why is one day more important than another, when all the daylight in the year is from the sun? (33:7).
By the Lord’s wisdom they were distinguished, and he appointed the different seasons and festivals. (33:8).
Some days he exalted and hallowed, and some he made ordinary days. (33:9).
All humans come from the ground, and humankind was created out of the dust. (33:10).
In the fullness of his knowledge the Lord distinguished them and appointed their different ways. (33:11).
Some he blessed and exalted, and some he made holy and brought near to himself, but some he cursed and brought low and turned them out of their place. (33:12).
Like clay in the hand of the potter, to be molded as he pleases, so are humans in the hand of their Maker, to be given whatever he decides. (33:13).
Good is the opposite of evil and life the opposite of death; so the sinner is the opposite of the godly. (33:14).
Look at all the works of the Most High; they come in pairs, one the opposite of the other. (33:15).
Now I was the last to keep vigil; I was like a gleaner following the grape-pickers; (33:16).
by the blessing of the Lord I arrived first, and like a grape-picker I filled my winepress. (33:17).
Consider that I have not labored for myself alone but for all who seek instruction. (33:18).
Hear me, you who are great among the people, and you leaders of the congregation, pay heed! (33:19).
To son or wife, to brother or friend, do not give power over yourself, as long as you live, and do not give your property to another, in case you change your mind and must ask for it. (33:20).
While you are still alive and have breath in you, do not let anyone take your place. (33:21).
For it is better that your children should ask from you than that you should look to the hand of your children. (33:22).
Excel in all that you do; bring no stain upon your honor. (33:23).
At the time when you end the days of your life, in the hour of death, distribute your inheritance. (33:24).
Fodder and a stick and burdens for a donkey; bread and discipline and work for a slave. (33:25).
Set your slaves to work, and you will find rest; leave their hands idle, and they will seek liberty. (33:26).
Yoke and strap will bow the neck, and for wicked slaves there are racks and tortures. (33:27).
Put them to work in order that they may not be idle, (33:28).
for idleness teaches much evil. (33:29).
Set them to work as is fitting for them, and if they do not obey make their fetters heavy. Do not be overbearing toward anyone, and do nothing without deliberation. (33:30).
If you have but one slave, treat him like yourself, because you have bought him with blood. If you have but one slave, treat him like a brother, for you will need him as you need your life. (33:31).
If you ill-treat him and he leaves you and runs away, (33:32).
which way will you go to seek him? (33:33).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 34
summaryBullets: The senseless have vain and false hopes, and dreams give wings to fools. (34:1).
As one who catches at a shadow and pursues the wind, so is anyone who pays attention to dreams. (34:2).
What is seen in dreams is but a reflection, the likeness of a face looking at itself. (34:3).
From an unclean thing, what can be clean? And from something false, what can be true? (34:4).
Divinations and omens and dreams are unreal, and like a woman in labor the mind has fantasies. (34:5).
Unless they are sent by intervention from the Most High, pay no attention to them. (34:6).
For dreams have deceived many, and those who put their hope in them have perished. (34:7).
Without such deceptions the law will be fulfilled, and wisdom is complete in a trustworthy mouth. (34:8).
People who have traveled know many things, and those with much experience know what they are talking about. (34:9).
The inexperienced know few things, (34:10).
but those who have traveled acquire much cleverness. (34:11).
I have seen many things in my travels, and I understand more than I can express. (34:12).
I have often been in danger of death but have escaped because of these experiences. (34:13).
The spirit of those who fear the Lord will live, (34:14).
for their hope is in him who saves them. (34:15).
Those who fear the Lord will not be timid or play the coward, for he is their hope. (34:16).
Happy are souls that fear the Lord! (34:17).
To whom do they look? And who is their support? (34:18).

The eyes of the Lord are on those who love him, a mighty shield and strong support, a shelter from scorching heat and a shade from noonday sun, a guard against stumbling and a help against falling. (34:19).
He lifts up the soul and makes the eyes sparkle; he gives health and life and blessing. (34:20).
If one sacrifices ill-gotten goods, the offering is blemished; (34:21).
the gifts of the lawless are not acceptable. (34:22).
The Most High is not pleased with the offerings of the ungodly, nor for a multitude of sacrifices does he forgive sins. (34:23).
Like one who kills a son before his father’s eyes is the person who offers a sacrifice from the property of the poor. (34:24).
The bread of the needy is the life of the poor; whoever deprives them of it is a murderer. (34:25).
To take away a neighbor’s living is to commit murder; (34:26).
to deprive an employee of wages is to shed blood. (34:27).
When one builds and another tears down, what do they gain but hard work? (34:28).
When one prays and another curses, to whose voice will the Lord listen? (34:29).
If one washes after touching a corpse and touches it again, what has been gained by washing? (34:30).
So if one fasts for his sins and goes again and does the same things, who will listen to his prayer? And what has he gained by humbling himself? (34:31).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 35
summaryBullets: The one who keeps the law makes many offerings; (35:1).
one who heeds the commandments makes an offering of well-being. (35:2).
The one who returns a kindness offers choice flour, (35:3).
and one who gives alms sacrifices a thank offering. (35:4).
To keep from wickedness is pleasing to the Lord, and to forsake unrighteousness is an atonement. (35:5).
Do not appear before the Lord empty-handed, (35:6).
for all that you offer is in fulfillment of the commandment. (35:7).
The offering of the righteous enriches the altar, and its pleasing odor rises before the Most High. (35:8).
The sacrifice of the righteous is acceptable, and it will never be forgotten. (35:9).
Be generous when you worship the Lord, and do not skimp the first fruits of your hands. (35:10).
With every gift show a cheerful face and dedicate your tithe with gladness. (35:11).
Give to the Most High as he has given to you and as generously as you can afford. (35:12).
For the Lord is the one who repays, and he will repay you sevenfold. (35:13).
Do not offer him a bribe, for he will not accept it, (35:14).
and do not rely on a dishonest sacrifice, for the Lord is the judge, and with him there is no partiality. (35:15).
He will not show partiality to the poor, but he will listen to the prayer of one who is wronged. (35:16).
He will not ignore the supplication of the orphan or the widow when she pours out her complaint. (35:17).
Do not the tears of the widow run down her cheek (35:18).
as she cries out against the one who causes them to fall? (35:19).
Those whose service is pleasing to the Lord will be accepted, and their prayers will reach to the clouds. (35:20).
The prayer of the humble pierces the clouds, and it will not rest until it reaches its goal; it will not desist until the Most High responds (35:21).
and does justice for the righteous and executes judgment. Indeed, the Lord will not delay, and like a warrior he will not be patient until he crushes the loins of the unmerciful (35:22).
and repays vengeance on the nations, until he destroys the multitude of the insolent and breaks the scepters of the unrighteous, (35:23).
until he repays mortals according to their deeds and the works of all according to their thoughts, (35:24).
until he judges the case of his people and makes them rejoice in his mercy. (35:25).
His mercy is as welcome in time of distress as clouds of rain in time of drought. (35:26).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 36
summaryBullets: Have mercy upon us, O God of all, (36:1).
and put all the nations in fear of you. (36:2).
Lift up your hand against foreign nations and let them see your might. (36:3).
As you have used us to show your holiness to them, so use them to show your glory to us. (36:4).
Then they will know, as we have known, that there is no God but you, O Lord. (36:5).
Give new signs and work other wonders; (36:6).
make your hand and right arm glorious. (36:7).
Rouse your anger and pour out your wrath; (36:8).
destroy the adversary and wipe out the enemy. (36:9).
Hasten the day, and remember the appointed time, and let people recount your mighty deeds. (36:10).
Let survivors be consumed in the fiery wrath, and may those who harm your people meet destruction. (36:11).
Crush the heads of hostile rulers who say, “There is no one but ourselves.” (36:12).
Gather all the tribes of Jacob, (36:13).
and give them their inheritance, as at the beginning. (36:16).
Have mercy, O Lord, on the people called by your name, on Israel, whom you have named your firstborn. (36:17).
Have pity on the city of your sanctuary, Jerusalem, the place of your dwelling. (36:18).
Fill Zion with your majesty and your temple with your glory. (36:19).
Bear witness to those whom you created in the beginning, and fulfill the prophecies spoken in your name. (36:20).
Reward those who wait for you, and let your prophets be found trustworthy. (36:21).
Hear, O Lord, the prayer of your servants, according to your goodwill toward your people, and all who are on the earth will know that you are the Lord, the God of the ages. (36:22).
The stomach will take any food, yet one food is better than another. (36:23).
As the palate tastes the kinds of game, so an intelligent mind detects false words. (36:24).
A perverse mind will cause grief, but a person with experience will pay him back. (36:25).
A woman will accept any man as a husband, but one daughter is preferable to another. (36:26).
A woman’s beauty lights up a man’s face, and there is nothing he desires more. (36:27).
If kindness and humility mark her speech, her husband is more fortunate than other men. (36:28).
He who acquires a wife gets his best possession, a helper fit for him and a pillar of support. (36:29).
Where there is no fence, the property will be plundered, and where there is no wife, a man will become a fugitive and a wanderer. (36:30).
For who will trust a nimble robber who skips from city to city? So who will trust a man who has no nest but lodges wherever nighttime finds him? (36:31).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 37
summaryBullets: Every friend says, “I, too, am a friend,” but some friends are friends only in name. (37:1).
Does not sorrow draw near to death when a companion and friend turns into an enemy? (37:2).
O inclination to evil, why were you formed to cover the land with deceit? (37:3).
Some companions rejoice in the happiness of friends, but in time of trouble they are against them. (37:4).
Some companions help a friend for their stomachs’ sake, yet in battle they will carry his shield. (37:5).
Do not forget friends during the battle, and do not be unmindful of them when you distribute your spoils. (37:6).
All counselors praise the counsel they give, but some give counsel in their own interest. (37:7).
Be wary of counselors and learn first what is their interest, for they will take thought for themselves. They may cast the lot against you (37:8).
and tell you, “Your way is good,” and then stand aside to see what happens to you. (37:9).
Do not consult the one who regards you with suspicion; hide your intentions from those who are jealous of you. (37:10).

Do not consult with a woman about her rival or with a coward about war, with a merchant about business or with a buyer about selling, with a miser about generosity or with the merciless about kindness, with an idler about any work or with a seasonal laborer about finishing the job, with a lazy slave about a big task— pay no attention to any advice they give. (37:11).
But associate with a godly person whom you know to be a keeper of the commandments, who is like-minded with yourself, and who will grieve with you if you fail. (37:12).
And heed the counsel of your own heart, for no one is more faithful to you than it is. (37:13).
For our own mind sometimes keeps us better informed than seven sentinels sitting high on a watchtower. (37:14).
But above all pray to the Most High that he may direct your way in truth. (37:15).
Discussion is the beginning of every work, and counsel precedes every undertaking. (37:16).
The mind is the root of all counsel; (37:17).
it sprouts four branches, good and evil, life and death, and it is the tongue that continually rules them. (37:18).
Some people may be clever enough to teach many and yet be useless to themselves. (37:19).
Skillful speakers may be hated; they will be destitute of all food, (37:20).
for the Lord has withheld the gift of charm, since they are lacking in all wisdom. (37:21).
If people are wise to their own advantage, the fruits of their good sense will be praiseworthy. (37:22).
The wise instruct their own people, and the fruits of their good sense are trustworthy. (37:23).
The wise will have praise heaped upon them, and all who see them will call them happy. (37:24).
The days of a person’s life are numbered, but the days of Israel are without number. (37:25).
Those who are wise among their people will inherit honor, and their names will live forever. (37:26).
My child, test yourself while you live; see what is bad for you, and do not give in to it. (37:27).
For not everything is good for everyone, and no one enjoys everything. (37:28).
Do not be greedy for every delicacy, and do not eat without restraint, (37:29).
for overeating brings sickness, and gluttony leads to nausea. (37:30).
Many have died of gluttony, but those who guard against it prolong their lives. (37:31).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 38
summaryBullets: Honor physicians for their services, for the Lord created them, (38:1).
for their gift of healing comes from the Most High, and they are rewarded by the king. (38:2).
The skill of physicians makes them distinguished, and in the presence of the great they are admired. (38:3).
The Lord created medicines out of the earth, and the sensible will not despise them. (38:4).
Was not water made sweet with a tree in order that its power might be known? (38:5).
And he gave skill to human beings that he might be glorified in his marvelous works. (38:6).
By them the physician heals and takes away pain; (38:7).
the pharmacist makes a mixture from them. God’s works will never be finished, and from him health spreads over all the earth. (38:8).
My child, when you are ill, do not delay, but pray to the Lord, and he will heal you. (38:9).
Give up your faults and direct your hands rightly, and cleanse your heart from all sin. (38:10).
Offer a sweet-smelling sacrifice and a memorial portion of choice flour, and pour oil on your offering, as much as you can afford. (38:11).
Then give physicians their place, for the Lord created them; do not let them leave you, for you need them. (38:12).
There may come a time when recovery lies in the hands of physicians, (38:13).
for they, too, pray to the Lord that he grant them success in diagnosis and in healing, for the sake of preserving life. (38:14).
Those who sin against their Maker will be defiant toward the physician. (38:15).
My child, let your tears fall for the dead, and as one in great pain begin the lament. Lay out the body according to custom, and do not neglect the burial. (38:16).
Let your weeping be bitter and your wailing fervent; make your mourning worthy of the departed, for one day or two, to avoid criticism; then be comforted for your grief. (38:17).
For grief may result in death, and a sorrowful heart saps one’s strength. (38:18).
In calamity, grief continues, but the life of the poor is a curse to the heart. (38:19).
Do not give your heart to grief; drive it away and remember your own end. (38:20).
Do not forget, there is no coming back; you do the dead no good, and you injure yourself. (38:21).
Remember his fate, for yours is like it; yesterday it was his, and today it is yours. (38:22).
When the dead are at rest, let their remembrance rest, too, and be comforted for them when their spirits have departed. (38:23).
The wisdom of the scribe depends on the opportunity of leisure; only the one who has little business can become wise. (38:24).
How can one become wise who handles the plow and who glories in the shaft of a goad, who drives oxen and is occupied with their work, and whose talk is about the offspring of bulls? (38:25).
He sets his heart on plowing furrows, and he loses sleep over fodder for the heifers. (38:26).

So it is with every artisan and master artisan who labors by night as well as by day; those who carve the signets of seals— each is diligent in making a great variety; they set their heart on painting a lifelike image, and they lose sleep in order to finish their work. (38:27).

So it is with the smith sitting by the anvil, intent on his ironwork; the breath of the fire melts his flesh, and he struggles with the heat of the furnace; the sound of the hammer deafens his ears, and his eyes are on the pattern of the object. He sets his heart on finishing his handiwork, and he loses sleep to complete its decoration. (38:28).
So it is with the potter sitting at his work and turning the wheel with his feet; he always lies down anxious about his work, and his every work is taken into account. (38:29).
He molds the clay with his arm and makes it pliable with his feet; he sets his heart to finish the glazing, and he takes care in firing the kiln. (38:30).
All these rely on their hands, and all are skillful in their own work. (38:31).
Without them no city can be inhabited, and wherever they live they will not go hungry. Yet they are not sought out for the council of the people, (38:32).

nor do they attain eminence in the public assembly. They do not sit in the judge’s seat, nor do they understand the decisions of the courts; they cannot expound discipline or judgment, and they are not found among the rulers. (38:33).
But they maintain the fabric of the world, and their concern is for the exercise of their trade. How different the one who devotes himself to the study of the law of the Most High! (38:34).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 39
summaryBullets: They seek out the wisdom of all the ancients and are concerned with prophecies; (39:1).
they preserve the sayings of the famous and penetrate the subtleties of parables; (39:2).
they seek out the hidden meanings of proverbs and are at home with the obscurities of parables. (39:3).
They serve among the great and appear before rulers; they travel in foreign nations and learn what is good and evil in the human lot. (39:4).
They set their hearts to rise early to seek the Lord who made them and to petition the Most High; they open their mouths in prayer and ask pardon for their sins. (39:5).
If the great Lord is willing, they will be filled with the spirit of understanding; they will pour forth words of wisdom of their own and give thanks to the Lord in prayer. (39:6).
The Lord will direct their counsel and knowledge as they meditate on his mysteries. (39:7).
They will show the discipline of their training and will glory in the law of the Lord’s covenant. (39:8).
Many will praise their understanding; it will never be blotted out. Their memory will not disappear, and their names will live through all generations. (39:9).
Nations will speak of their wisdom, and the congregation will proclaim their praise. (39:10).
If they live long, they will leave a name greater than a thousand, and if they go to rest, it is enough for them. (39:11).
I have more on my mind to express; I am full like the full moon. (39:12).
Listen to me, my faithful children, and blossom like a rose growing by a stream of water. (39:13).
Send out fragrance like incense and put forth blossoms like a lily. Raise your voice and sing a hymn of praise; bless the Lord for all his works. (39:14).
Ascribe majesty to his name and give thanks to him with praise, with songs on your lips and with harps; this is what you shall say in thanksgiving: (39:15).
“All the works of the Lord are very good, and whatever he commands will be done at the appointed time. (39:16).

No one can say, ‘What is this?’ or ‘Why is that?’— for at the appointed time everything will be made known. At his word the waters stood in a heap and the reservoirs of water at the word of his mouth. (39:17).
At his command, his purpose is fulfilled, and none can limit his saving power. (39:18).
The works of all are before him, and nothing can be hidden from his eyes. (39:19).
From age to age he observes all, and nothing is too marvelous for him. (39:20).
No one can say, ‘What is this?’ or ‘Why is that?’— for everything has been created for its own purpose. (39:21).
“His blessing covers the dry land like a river and drenches it like a flood. (39:22).
The nations will inherit his wrath, as when he turned a watered land into salt. (39:23).
To the faithful his ways are straight but full of pitfalls for the lawless. (39:24).
From the beginning good things were created for the good but for sinners good things and bad. (39:25).
The basic necessities of human life are water and fire and iron and salt and wheat flour and milk and honey, the blood of the grape and oil and clothing. (39:26).
All these are good for the godly, but for sinners they turn into evils. (39:27).
“There are winds created for vengeance, and in their anger they can dislodge mountains; on the day of reckoning they will pour out their strength and calm the anger of their Maker. (39:28).
Fire and hail and famine and pestilence— all these have been created for vengeance; (39:29).
the fangs of wild animals and scorpions and vipers and the sword that punishes the ungodly with destruction. (39:30).
They take delight in doing his bidding, always ready for his service on earth, and when their time comes they never disobey his command.” (39:31).
So from the beginning I have been steadfast and have thought it out and left it in writing: (39:32).
All the works of the Lord are good, and he will supply every need in its time. (39:33).
No one can say, “This is not as good as that,” for everything proves good in its appointed time. (39:34).
So now sing praise with all your heart and voice, and bless the name of the Lord. (39:35).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 40
summaryBullets: Hard work was created for everyone, and a heavy yoke is laid on the children of Adam, from the day they come forth from their mother’s womb until the day they return to the mother of all the living. (40:1).
Perplexities and fear of heart are theirs and anxious thought of the day of their death. (40:2).
From the one who sits on a splendid throne to the one who grovels in dust and ashes, (40:3).
from the one who wears purple and a crown to the one who is clothed in burlap, (40:4).
there is anger and envy and trouble and unrest and fear of death and fury and strife. And when one rests upon his bed, his sleep at night confuses his mind. (40:5).
He gets little or no rest; he struggles in his sleep as he did by day. He is troubled by the visions of his mind like one who has escaped from the battlefield. (40:6).
At the moment he reaches safety he wakes up, astonished that his fears were groundless. (40:7).
To all creatures, human and animal, but to sinners seven times more, (40:8).
come death and bloodshed and strife and sword, calamities and famine and ruin and plague. (40:9).
All these were created for the lawless, and on their account the flood came. (40:10).
All that is of earth returns to earth, and what is from above returns above. (40:11).
All bribery and injustice will be blotted out, but good faith will last forever. (40:12).
The wealth of the unjust will dry up like a river and crash like a loud clap of thunder in a storm. (40:13).
As a generous person has cause to rejoice, so lawbreakers will utterly fail. (40:14).
The children of the ungodly put out few branches; they are unhealthy roots on sheer rock. (40:15).
The reeds by any water or river bank are plucked up before any grass, (40:16).
but kindness is like a garden of blessings, and almsgiving endures forever. (40:17).
A life of abundance and wages make life sweet, but better than either is finding a treasure. (40:18).

Children and the building of a city establish one’s name, but better than either is the one who finds wisdom. Cattle and orchards make one prosperous, but a blameless wife is accounted better than either. (40:19).
Wine and music gladden the heart, but the love of friends is better than either. (40:20).
The flute and the harp make sweet melody, but a pleasant voice is better than either. (40:21).
The eye desires grace and beauty, but the green shoots of grain more than either. (40:22).
A friend or companion is always welcome, but a sensible wife is better than either. (40:23).
Kindred and helpers are for a time of trouble, but almsgiving rescues better than either. (40:24).
Gold and silver make one stand firm, but good counsel is esteemed more than either. (40:25).
Riches and strength build up confidence, but the fear of the Lord is better than either. There is no want in the fear of the Lord, and with it there is no need to seek for help. (40:26).
The fear of the Lord is like a garden of blessing and covers a person better than any glory. (40:27).
My child, do not lead the life of a beggar; it is better to die than to beg. (40:28).

When one looks to the table of another, one’s way of life cannot be considered a life. One loses self-respect with another person’s food, but one who is intelligent and well instructed guards against that. (40:29).
In the mouth of the shameless begging is sweet, but it kindles a fire inside them. (40:30).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 41
summaryBullets: O death, how bitter is the thought of you to the one at peace among possessions, who has nothing to worry about and is prosperous in everything and still is vigorous enough to enjoy pleasure! (41:1).
O death, how welcome is your sentence to one who is needy and failing in strength, worn down by age and anxious about everything, to one who is contrary and has lost all patience! (41:2).
Do not fear death’s decree for you; remember those who went before you and those who will come after. (41:3).

This is the Lord’s decree for all flesh; why, then, should you reject the will of the Most High? Whether life lasts for ten years or a hundred or a thousand, there are no questions asked in Hades. (41:4).
The children of sinners are abominable children, and they frequent the haunts of the ungodly. (41:5).
The inheritance of the children of sinners will perish, and on their offspring will be a perpetual disgrace. (41:6).
Children will blame an ungodly father, for they suffer disgrace because of him. (41:7).
Woe to you, the ungodly, who have forsaken the law of the Most High! (41:8).
You will beget them only for groaning. When you stumble, there is lasting joy, and when you die, a curse is your lot. (41:9).
Whatever comes from earth returns to earth, so the ungodly go from curse to destruction. (41:10).
The breath of humans is in their bodies, but a virtuous name will never be blotted out. (41:11).
Have regard for your name, since it will outlive you longer than a thousand hoards of gold. (41:12).
The days of a good life are numbered, but a good name lasts forever. (41:13).
My children, be true to your training and be at peace; hidden wisdom and unseen treasure— of what value is either? (41:14).
Better are those who hide their folly than those who hide their wisdom. (41:15).
Therefore show respect for my words, for it is not good to feel shame in every circumstance, nor is every kind of shaming to be approved. (41:16).
Be ashamed of sexual immorality before your father or mother and of a lie before a prince or a ruler, (41:17).
of a crime before a judge or magistrate and of a breach of the law before the congregation and the people, of unjust dealing before your partner or your friend (41:18).
and of theft in the place where you live. Be ashamed of breaking an oath or agreement and of leaning on your elbow at meals, of surliness in receiving or giving (41:19).
and of silence before those who greet you, of looking at a prostitute (41:20).
and of rejecting the appeal of a relative, of taking away someone’s portion or gift and of gazing at another man’s wife, (41:21).
of meddling with his female servant— and do not approach her bed; of abusive words, before friends— and do not be insulting after making a gift. (41:22).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 42
summaryBullets: Be ashamed of repeating what you hear and of betraying secrets. Then you will show proper shame and will find favor with everyone. Of the following things do not be ashamed, and do not sin by showing partiality: (42:1).
Do not be ashamed of the law of the Most High and his covenant and of rendering judgment to acquit the ungodly; (42:2).
of keeping accounts with a partner or with traveling companions and of dividing the inheritance of friends; (42:3).
of accuracy with scales and weights and of acquiring much or little; (42:4).
of profit from dealing with merchants and of frequent disciplining of children and of drawing blood from the back of a wicked slave. (42:5).
Where there is an untrustworthy wife, a seal is a good thing, and where there are many hands, lock things up. (42:6).
When you make a deposit, be sure it is counted and weighed, and when you give or receive, put it all in writing. (42:7).
Do not be ashamed to correct the stupid or foolish or the aged who are guilty of sexual immorality. Then you will show your sound training and will be approved by all. (42:8).
A daughter is a secret anxiety to her father, and worry over her robs him of sleep; when she is young, for fear she may not marry, or if married, for fear she may be disliked; (42:9).
while a virgin, for fear she may be seduced and become pregnant in her father’s house; or having a husband, for fear she may go astray, or, though married, for fear she may be barren. (42:10).

Keep strict watch over a headstrong daughter, or she may make you a laughingstock to your enemies, a byword in the city and the assembly of the people, and put you to shame in public gatherings. See that there is no lattice in her room, no spot that overlooks the approaches to the house. (42:11).
Do not let her parade her beauty before any man or spend her time among married women, (42:12).
for from garments comes the moth and from a woman comes woman’s wickedness. (42:13).
Better is the wickedness of a man than a woman who does good; it is a woman who brings shame and disgrace. (42:14).
I will now call to mind the works of the Lord and will declare what I have seen. By the word of the Lord his works are made, and all his creatures do his will. (42:15).
The sun looks down on everything with its light, and the work of the Lord is full of his glory. (42:16).
The Lord has not empowered even his holy ones to recount all his marvelous works, which the Lord the Almighty has established so that the universe may stand firm in his glory. (42:17).
He searches out the abyss and the human heart; he understands their subtleties. For the Most High knows all that may be known; he sees from of old the things that are to come. (42:18).
He discloses what has been and what is to be, and he reveals the traces of hidden things. (42:19).
No thought escapes him, and not a single word is hidden from him. (42:20).
He has set in order the splendors of his wisdom; he is from all eternity one and the same. Nothing can be added or taken away, and he needs no one to be his counselor. (42:21).
How desirable are all his works, and how sparkling they are to see! (42:22).
All these things live and remain forever; each creature is preserved to meet a particular need. (42:23).
All things come in pairs, one opposite the other, and he has made nothing incomplete. (42:24).
Each supplements the virtues of the other. Who could ever tire of seeing his glory? (42:25).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 43
summaryBullets: The pride of the higher realms is the clear vault of the sky, as glorious to behold as the sight of the heavens. (43:1).
The sun, when it appears, proclaims as it rises what a marvelous instrument it is, the work of the Most High. (43:2).
At noon it parches the land, and who can withstand its burning heat? (43:3).

A man tending a furnace works in burning heat, but three times as hot is the sun scorching the mountains; when it breathes out fiery vapors and when it shines forth its rays, it blinds the eyes. (43:4).
Great is the Lord who made it; at his orders it hurries on its course. (43:5).
It is the moon that marks the changing seasons, governing the times, an everlasting sign. (43:6).
From the moon comes the sign for festal days, a light that wanes when it completes its course. (43:7).
The new moon, as its name suggests, renews itself; how marvelous it is in this change, a beacon to the hosts on high shining in the vault of the heavens! (43:8).
The glory of the stars is the beauty of heaven, a glittering array in the heights of the Lord. (43:9).
On the orders of the Holy One they stand in their appointed places; they never relax in their watches. (43:10).
Look at the rainbow and praise him who made it; it is exceedingly beautiful in its brightness. (43:11).
It encircles the sky with its glorious arc; the hands of the Most High have stretched it out. (43:12).
By his command he sends the driving snow and speeds the lightnings of his judgment. (43:13).
Therefore the storehouses are opened, and the clouds fly out like birds. (43:14).
In his majesty he gives the clouds their strength, and the hailstones are broken in pieces. (43:15).
when he appears, the mountains shake. At his will the south wind blows, (43:16).

The voice of his thunder causes the earth to tremble; so do the storm from the north and the whirlwind. He scatters the snow like birds flying down, and its descent is like locusts alighting. (43:17).
The eye is dazzled by the beauty of its whiteness, and the mind is amazed as it falls. (43:18).
He pours frost over the earth like salt, and icicles form like pointed thorns. (43:19).
The cold north wind blows, and ice freezes on the water; it settles on every pool of water, and the water puts it on like a breastplate. (43:20).
He consumes the mountains and burns up the wilderness and withers the tender grass like fire. (43:21).
A mist quickly heals all things; the falling dew gives refreshment from the heat. (43:22).
By his plan he stilled the deep and planted islands in it. (43:23).
Those who sail the sea tell of its dangers, and we marvel at what we hear. (43:24).
In it are strange and marvelous creatures, all kinds of living things, and mighty sea monsters. (43:25).
Because of him each of his messengers succeeds, and by his word all things hold together. (43:26).
We could say more but could never say enough; let the final word be: “He is the all.” (43:27).
Where can we find the strength to praise him? For he is greater than all his works. (43:28).
Awesome is the Lord and very great, and marvelous is his power. (43:29).
Glorify the Lord and exalt him as much as you can, for he surpasses even that. When you exalt him, summon all your strength, and do not grow weary, for you cannot praise him enough. (43:30).
Who has seen him and can describe him? Or who can extol him as he is? (43:31).
Many things greater than these lie hidden, for I have seen but few of his works. (43:32).
For the Lord has made all things, and to the godly he has given wisdom. (43:33).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 44
summaryBullets: Let us now sing the praises of famous men, our ancestors in their generations. (44:1).
The Lord apportioned to them great glory, his majesty from the beginning. (44:2).
There were those who ruled in their kingdoms and made a name for themselves by their strength; those who gave counsel because they were intelligent; those who spoke in prophetic oracles; (44:3).
those who led the people by their counsels and by their knowledge of the people’s lore; they were wise in their words of instruction; (44:4).
those who composed musical tunes or put verses in writing; (44:5).
rich men endowed with resources, living peacefully in their homes— (44:6).
all these were honored in their generations and were the pride of their times. (44:7).
Some of them have left behind a name, so that others declare their praise. (44:8).
But of others there is no memory; they have perished as though they had never existed; they have become as though they had never been born, they and their children after them. (44:9).
But these also were men of compassion whose righteous deeds have not been forgotten; (44:10).
their wealth will remain with their descendants and their inheritance with their children’s children. (44:11).
Their descendants stand by the covenants; their children also, for their sake. (44:12).
Their offspring will continue forever, and their glory will never be blotted out. (44:13).
Their bodies are buried in peace, but their name lives on generation after generation. (44:14).
The assembly declares their wisdom, and the congregation proclaims their praise. (44:15).
Enoch pleased the Lord and was taken up, an example of repentance to all generations. (44:16).
Noah was found perfect and righteous; in the time of wrath he kept humanity alive; because of him a remnant was left on the earth when the flood came. (44:17).
Everlasting covenants were made with him that all flesh should never again be blotted out by a flood. (44:18).
Abraham was the great father of a multitude of nations, and no one has been found like him in glory. (44:19).
He kept the law of the Most High and entered into a covenant with him; he certified the covenant in his flesh, and when he was tested he proved faithful. (44:20).

Therefore the Lord assured him with an oath that the nations would be blessed through his offspring, that he would make him as numerous as the dust of the earth and exalt his offspring like the stars and give them an inheritance from sea to sea and from the Euphrates to the ends of the earth. (44:21).
To Isaac also he gave the same assurance for the sake of his father Abraham. The blessing of all people and a covenant (44:22).

he made to rest on the head of Jacob; he acknowledged him with his blessings and gave him his inheritance; he divided his portions and distributed them among twelve tribes. From his descendants the Lord brought forth a man of compassion who found favor in the sight of all (44:23).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 45
summaryBullets: and was beloved by God and people, Moses, whose memory is blessed. (45:1).
He made him equal in glory to the holy ones and made him great, to the terror of his enemies. (45:2).
By his words he performed swift miracles; the Lord glorified him in the presence of kings. He gave him commandments for his people and revealed to him his glory. (45:3).
For his faithfulness and meekness he consecrated him, choosing him out of all humankind. (45:4).

He allowed him to hear his voice and led him into the dark cloud and gave him the commandments face to face, the law of life and knowledge, so that he might teach Jacob the covenant and Israel his decrees. (45:5).
He exalted Aaron, a holy man like Moses, who was his brother, of the tribe of Levi. (45:6).
He made an everlasting covenant with him and gave him the priesthood of the people. He blessed him with stateliness and put a glorious robe on him. (45:7).
He clothed him in perfect splendor and strengthened him with the apparel of authority, the linen undergarments, the long robe, and the ephod. (45:8).
And he encircled him with pomegranates, with many golden bells all around, to send forth a sound as he walked, to make their ringing heard in the temple as a reminder to his people; (45:9).
with the sacred vestment, of gold and violet and purple, the work of an embroiderer; with the oracle of judgment, the manifestations of truth; (45:10).

with twisted crimson, the work of an artisan; with precious stones engraved like seals, in a setting of gold, the work of a jeweler, to commemorate in engraved letters each of the tribes of Israel; (45:11).
with a gold crown upon his turban, inscribed like a holy seal, majestic and glorious, a work of power, a delight to the eyes, richly adorned. (45:12).
Before him such beautiful things did not exist. No outsider ever put them on, but only his sons and his descendants in perpetuity. (45:13).
His sacrifices shall be wholly burned twice every day continually. (45:14).

Moses ordained him and anointed him with holy oil; it was an everlasting covenant for him and for his descendants as long as the heavens endure, to minister to the Lord and serve as priest and bless his people in his name. (45:15).
He chose him out of all the living to offer sacrifice to the Lord, incense and a pleasing odor as a memorial, to make atonement for the people. (45:16).
In his commandments he gave him authority, by means of a decree, and judgments, to teach Jacob the testimonies and to enlighten Israel with his law. (45:17).
Outsiders conspired against him and envied him in the wilderness, Dathan and Abiram and their followers and the company of Korah, in wrath and anger. (45:18).
The Lord saw it and was not pleased, and in the heat of his anger they were destroyed; he performed wonders against them to consume them in flaming fire. (45:19).
He added glory to Aaron and gave him a heritage; he allotted to him the best of the first fruits and prepared bread of first fruits in abundance, (45:20).
for they eat the sacrifices of the Lord, which he gave to him and his descendants. (45:21).
But in the land of the people he has no inheritance, and he has no portion among the people, for the Lord himself is his portion and inheritance. (45:22).

Phinehas son of Eleazar ranks third in glory for being zealous in the fear of the Lord and standing firm, when the people turned away, in the noble courage of his soul, and he made atonement for Israel. (45:23).

Therefore a covenant of peace was established with him, that he should be leader of the sanctuary and of his people, that he and his descendants should have the dignity of the priesthood forever. (45:24).
Just as a covenant was established with David son of Jesse of the tribe of Judah, that the king’s heritage passes only from son to son, so the heritage of Aaron is for his descendants alone. (45:25).

And now bless the Lord who has crowned you with glory. May the Lord grant you wisdom of mind to judge his people with justice, so that their prosperity may not vanish and that their glory may endure through all their generations. (45:26).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 46
summaryBullets: Joshua son of Nun was mighty in war and was the successor of Moses in the prophetic office. He became, as his name implies, a great savior of God’s elect, to take vengeance on the enemies who rose against them, so that he might give Israel its inheritance. (46:1).
How glorious he was when he lifted his hands and brandished his sword against the cities! (46:2).
Who before him ever stood so firm? For he waged the wars of the Lord. (46:3).
Was it not through him that the sun stood still and one day became as long as two? (46:4).
He called upon the Most High, the Mighty One, when enemies pressed him on every side, and the great Lord answered him with hailstones of mighty power. (46:5).

He overwhelmed that nation in battle, and on the slope he destroyed his opponents, so that the nations might know his armament, because their battle was against the Lord, for he was a devoted follower of the Mighty One. (46:6).
And in the days of Moses he showed compassion, he and Caleb son of Jephunneh: they opposed the congregation, restrained the people from sin, and stilled their wicked grumbling. (46:7).
And these two alone were spared out of six hundred thousand infantry, to lead the people into their inheritance, the land flowing with milk and honey. (46:8).
The Lord gave Caleb strength, which remained with him in his old age, so that he went up to the hill country, and his children obtained it for an inheritance, (46:9).
so that all the Israelites might see how good it is to follow the Lord. (46:10).
The judges also, with their respective names, whose hearts did not fall into idolatry and who did not turn away from the Lord— may their memory be blessed! (46:11).
May their bones send forth new life from where they lie, and may the names of those who have been honored live again in their children! (46:12).
Samuel was beloved by his Lord; a prophet of the Lord, he established the kingdom and anointed rulers over his people. (46:13).
By the law of the Lord he judged the congregation, and the Lord watched over Jacob. (46:14).
By his faithfulness he was proved to be a prophet, and by his words he became known as a trustworthy seer. (46:15).
He called upon the Lord, the Mighty One, when his enemies pressed him on every side, and he offered in sacrifice a suckling lamb. (46:16).
Then the Lord thundered from heaven and made his voice heard with a mighty sound; (46:17).
he subdued the leaders of the enemy and all the rulers of the Philistines. (46:18).
Before the time of his eternal sleep, Samuel bore witness before the Lord and his anointed: “No property, not so much as a pair of shoes, have I taken from anyone!” And no one accused him. (46:19).
Even after he had fallen asleep, he prophesied and made known to the king his death and lifted up his voice from the ground in prophecy, to blot out the lawlessness of the people. (46:20).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 47
summaryBullets: After him Nathan rose up to prophesy in the days of David. (47:1).
As the fat is set apart from the offering of well-being, so David was set apart from the Israelites. (47:2).
He played with lions as though they were young goats and with bears as though they were lambs of the flock. (47:3).
In his youth did he not kill a giant and take away the people’s disgrace, when he whirled the stone in the sling and struck down the boasting Goliath? (47:4).
For he called on the Lord, the Most High, and he gave strength to his right arm to strike down a mighty warrior and to exalt the power of his people. (47:5).
So they glorified him for the tens of thousands and praised him for the blessings bestowed by the Lord, when the glorious diadem was given to him. (47:6).
For he wiped out his enemies on every side and scorned his adversaries the Philistines; he crushed their power to our own day. (47:7).
In all that he did he gave thanks to the Holy One, the Most High, proclaiming his glory; he sang praise with all his heart, and he loved his Maker. (47:8).
He placed singers before the altar, to make sweet melody with their voices. (47:9).
He gave beauty to the festivals and arranged their times throughout the year, while they praised God’s holy name and the sanctuary resounded from early morning. (47:10).
The Lord took away his sins and exalted his power forever; he gave him a covenant of kingship and a glorious throne in Israel. (47:11).
After him a wise son rose up who because of him lived in security: (47:12).
Solomon reigned in an age of peace, because God gave him rest all around, so that he might build a house in his name and provide a sanctuary to stand forever. (47:13).
How wise you were when you were young! You overflowed like the Nile with understanding. (47:14).
Your influence spread throughout the earth, and you filled it with proverbs having deep meaning. (47:15).
Your fame reached to far-off islands, and you were loved for your peaceful reign. (47:16).
For your songs, proverbs, parables, and understanding the nations marveled at you. (47:17).
In the name of the Lord God, who is called the God of Israel, you gathered gold like tin and amassed silver like lead. (47:18).
But you brought in women to lie at your side, and through your body you were brought into subjection. (47:19).
You stained your honor and defiled your family line, so that you brought wrath upon your children, and they were grieved at your folly, (47:20).
because the sovereignty was divided and a rebel kingdom arose out of Ephraim. (47:21).

But the Lord will never give up his mercy or cause any of his words to perish; he will never blot out the descendants of his chosen one or destroy the family line of him who loved him. So he gave a remnant to Jacob and to David a root from his own family. (47:22).

Solomon rested with his ancestors and left behind him one of his sons broad in folly and lacking in sense, Rehoboam, whose policy drove the people to revolt. Then Jeroboam son of Nebat led Israel into sin and started Ephraim on its sinful ways. (47:23).
Their sins increased more and more until they were exiled from their land. (47:24).
For they sought out every kind of wickedness until vengeance came upon them. (47:25).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 48
summaryBullets: Then Elijah arose, a prophet like fire, and his word burned like a torch. (48:1).
He brought a famine upon them, and by his zeal he made them few in number. (48:2).
By the word of the Lord he shut up the heavens and also three times brought down fire. (48:3).
How glorious you were, Elijah, in your wondrous deeds! Who can boast as you can? (48:4).
You who raised a corpse from death and from Hades, by the word of the Most High, (48:5).
who sent kings down to destruction and famous men from their sickbeds, (48:6).
who heard rebuke at Sinai and judgments of vengeance at Horeb, (48:7).
who anointed kings to inflict retribution and prophets to succeed you, (48:8).
who were taken up by a whirlwind of fire in a chariot with horses of fire, (48:9).
who were prepared at the appointed time to calm wrath before it breaks out in fury, to turn the hearts of parents to their children and to restore the tribes of Jacob. (48:10).
Happy are those who saw you and were adorned in love! For we also shall surely live. (48:11).

When Elijah was enveloped in the whirlwind, Elisha was filled with his spirit. He performed twice as many signs and marvels with every utterance of his mouth. Never in his lifetime did he tremble before any ruler, nor could anyone intimidate him at all. (48:12).
Nothing was too hard for him, and when he was dead his body prophesied. (48:13).
In his life he did wonders, and in death his deeds were marvelous. (48:14).

Despite all this the people did not repent, nor did they forsake their sins, until they were carried off as plunder from their land and were scattered over all the earth. The people were left very few in number but with a ruler from the house of David. (48:15).
Some of them did what was right, but others sinned more and more. (48:16).
Hezekiah fortified his city and brought water into its midst; he tunneled the rock with iron tools and built cisterns for the water. (48:17).
In his days Sennacherib invaded the country; he sent his commander and departed; he shook his fist against Zion and made great boasts in his arrogance. (48:18).
Then their hearts and hands were shaken, and they were in anguish, like women in labor. (48:19).
But they called upon the Lord who is merciful, spreading out their hands toward him. The Holy One quickly heard them from heaven and delivered them through Isaiah. (48:20).
The Lord struck down the camp of the Assyrians, and his angel wiped them out. (48:21).
For Hezekiah did what was pleasing to the Lord, and he kept firmly to the ways of his ancestor David, as he was commanded by the prophet Isaiah, who was great and trustworthy in his visions. (48:22).
In Isaiah’s days the sun went backward, and he prolonged the life of the king. (48:23).
By his dauntless spirit he saw the future and comforted the mourners in Zion. (48:24).
He revealed what was to occur to the end of time and the hidden things before they happened. (48:25).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 49
summaryBullets: The name of Josiah is like blended incense prepared by the skill of the perfumer; his memory is as sweet as honey to every mouth and like music at a banquet of wine. (49:1).
He did what was right by reforming the people and removing the lawless abominations. (49:2).
He kept his heart fixed on the Lord; in lawless times he made godliness prevail. (49:3).
Except for David and Hezekiah and Josiah, all of them were great sinners, for they abandoned the law of the Most High; the kings of Judah came to an end. (49:4).
They gave their power to others and their glory to a foreign nation, (49:5).
who set fire to the chosen city of the sanctuary and made its streets desolate, as Jeremiah had foretold. (49:6).
For they had mistreated him, who even in the womb had been consecrated a prophet, to pluck up and ruin and destroy and likewise to build and to plant. (49:7).
It was Ezekiel who saw the vision of glory, which God showed him above the chariot of the cherubim. (49:8).
For he also mentioned Job, who held fast to all the ways of justice. (49:9).
May the bones of the Twelve Prophets send forth new life from where they lie, for they comforted the people of Jacob and delivered them with confident hope. (49:10).
How shall we magnify Zerubbabel? He was like a signet ring on the right hand, (49:11).
and so was Jeshua son of Jozadak; in their days they built the house and raised a temple holy to the Lord, prepared for everlasting glory. (49:12).
The memory of Nehemiah also is lasting; he raised our fallen walls and set up gates and bars and rebuilt our ruined houses. (49:13).
Few have ever been created on earth like Enoch, for he was taken up from the earth. (49:14).
Nor was anyone ever born like Joseph; even his bones were cared for. (49:15).
Shem and Seth and Enosh were honored, but above every other created living being was Adam. (49:16).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 50
summaryBullets: The leader of his brothers and the pride of his people was the high priest, Simon son of Onias, who in his life repaired the house and in his time fortified the temple. (50:1).
He laid the foundations for the high double walls, the high retaining walls for the temple enclosure. (50:2).
In his days a water cistern was dug, a reservoir like the sea in circumference. (50:3).
He considered how to save his people from ruin and fortified the city against siege. (50:4).
How glorious he was as he gazed from the tent, as he came out of the house of the curtain, (50:5).
like the morning star among the clouds, like the full moon at the festal season, (50:6).
like the sun shining on the temple of the Most High, like the rainbow gleaming in splendid clouds, (50:7).
like roses in the days of the spring harvest, like lilies by springs of water, like a green shoot on Lebanon on a summer day, (50:8).
like fire and incense in the censer, like a vessel of hammered gold studded with all kinds of precious stones, (50:9).
like an olive tree laden with fruit, and like a cypress towering in the clouds. (50:10).
When he put on his glorious robe and clothed himself in perfect splendor, when he went up to the holy altar, he made the court of the sanctuary glorious. (50:11).

When he received the portions from the hands of the priests, as he stood by the hearth of the altar with a garland of brothers around him, he was like a young cedar on Lebanon surrounded by the trunks of palm trees. (50:12).
All the sons of Aaron in their splendor held the Lord’s offering in their hands before the whole congregation of Israel. (50:13).
Finishing the service at the altars and arranging the offering to the Most High, the Almighty, (50:14).
he held out his hand for the cup and poured a drink offering of the blood of the grape; he poured it out at the foot of the altar, a pleasing odor to the Most High, the king of all. (50:15).
Then the sons of Aaron shouted; they blew their trumpets of hammered metal; they sounded a mighty fanfare as a reminder before the Most High. (50:16).
Then all the people together quickly fell to the ground on their faces to worship their Lord, the Almighty, God Most High. (50:17).
Then the singers praised him with their voices in sweet and full-toned melody. (50:18).
And the people of the Lord Most High offered their prayer before the Merciful One, until the order of worship of the Lord was ended and they completed his ritual. (50:19).
Then Simon came down and raised his hands over the whole congregation of Israelites, to pronounce the blessing of the Lord with his lips and to glory in his name, (50:20).
and they bowed down in worship a second time to receive the blessing from the Most High. (50:21).
And now bless the God of all, who everywhere works great wonders, who exalts our days from birth and deals with us according to his mercy. (50:22).
May he give us gladness of heart, and may there be peace in our days in Israel, as in the days of old. (50:23).
May he entrust to us his mercy, and may he deliver us in our days! (50:24).
Two nations my soul detests, and the third is not even a nation: (50:25).
those who live in Seir and the Philistines and the foolish people who live in Shechem. (50:26).
Instruction in understanding and knowledge I have written in this book, Jesus son of Eleazar son of Sirach of Jerusalem, whose mind poured forth wisdom. (50:27).
Happy are those who concern themselves with these things, and those who lay them to heart will become wise. (50:28).
For if they put them into practice, they will be equal to anything, for the fear of the Lord is their path. (50:29).

stories.title: 📜 Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 51
summaryBullets: I give you thanks, O Lord and King, and praise you, O God my Savior. I give thanks to your name, (51:1).

for you have been my protector and helper and have delivered my body from destruction and from the trap laid by a slanderous tongue, from lips that fabricate lies. In the face of my adversaries, you have been my helper (51:2).
and delivered me, in the greatness of your mercy and of your name, from grinding teeth about to devour me, from the hand of those seeking my life, from the many troubles I endured, (51:3).
from choking fire on every side, and from the midst of fire that I had not kindled, (51:4).
from the deep belly of Hades, from an unclean tongue and lying words, (51:5).
the slander of an unrighteous tongue to the king. My soul drew near to death, and my life was on the brink of Hades below. (51:6).
They surrounded me on every side, and there was no one to help me. I looked for human assistance, and there was none. (51:7).
Then I remembered your mercy, O Lord, and your kindness from of old, for you rescue those who wait for you and save them from the hand of their enemies. (51:8).
And I sent up my prayer from the earth and begged for rescue from death. (51:9).
I cried out, “Lord, you are my Father; do not forsake me in the days of trouble, when there is no help against the proud. (51:10).
I will praise your name continually and will sing hymns of thanksgiving.” My prayer was heard, (51:11).

for you saved me from destruction and rescued me in time of trouble. For this reason I thank you and praise you, and I bless the name of the Lord. ——— Give thanks to the Lord , for he is good, for his steadfast love endures forever. Give thanks to the God of praises, for his steadfast love endures forever. Give thanks to the guardian of Israel, for his steadfast love endures forever. Give thanks to him who formed all things, for his steadfast love endures forever. Give thanks to the redeemer of Israel, for his steadfast love endures forever. Give thanks to him who gathers the dispersed of Israel, for his steadfast love endures forever. Give thanks to him who rebuilt his city and his sanctuary, for his steadfast love endures forever. Give thanks to him who makes a horn to sprout for the house of David, for his steadfast love endures forever. Give thanks to him who has chosen the sons of Zadok to be priests, for his steadfast love endures forever. Give thanks to the shield of Abraham, for his steadfast love endures forever. Give thanks to the rock of Isaac, for his steadfast love endures forever. Give thanks to the mighty one of Jacob, for his steadfast love endures forever. Give thanks to him who has chosen Zion, for his steadfast love endures forever. Give thanks to the King of the kings of kings, for his steadfast love endures forever. He has raised up a horn for his people, praise for all his loyal ones. For the children of Israel, the people close to him. Praise the Lord ! ——— (51:12).
While I was still young, before I went on my travels, I sought wisdom openly in my prayer. (51:13).
Before the temple I asked for her, and I will search for her until the end. (51:14).
From the first blossom to the ripening grape, my heart delighted in her; my foot walked on the straight path; from my youth I followed her steps. (51:15).
I inclined my ear a little and received her, and I found for myself much instruction. (51:16).
I made progress in her; to him who gives wisdom I will give glory. (51:17).
For I resolved to practice wisdom, and I was zealous for the good, and I shall never be disappointed. (51:18).
My soul grappled with wisdom, and in my conduct I was strict. I spread out my hands to the heavens and lamented my ignorance of her. (51:19).
I directed my soul to her, and in purity I found her. With her I gained understanding from the first; therefore I will never be forsaken. (51:20).
My heart was stirred to seek her; therefore I have gained a prize possession. (51:21).
The Lord gave me my tongue as a reward, and I will praise him with it. (51:22).
Draw near to me, you who are uneducated, and lodge in the house of instruction. (51:23).
Why do you say you are lacking in these things, and why do you endure such great thirst? (51:24).
I opened my mouth and said, “Acquire wisdom for yourselves without money. (51:25).
“Put your neck under her yoke, and let your souls receive instruction; it is to be found close by.” (51:26).
See with your own eyes that I have labored but little and found for myself much serenity. (51:27).
Hear but a little of my instruction, and through me you will acquire silver and gold. (51:28).
May your soul rejoice in God’s mercy, and may you never be ashamed to praise him. (51:29).
Do your work in good time, and in his own time God will give you your reward. (51:30).
